"""Tests for PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator."""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pytest

from sklearn.datasets import make_classification, make_regression
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.inspection import PartialDependenceDisplay
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, LogisticRegression


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def close_matplotlib_figures():
    """Keep tests independent and avoid matplotlib's open-figure warning."""
    yield
    plt.close("all")


@pytest.fixture
def regression_data():
    X, y = make_regression(n_samples=40, n_features=3, random_state=0)
    return LinearRegression().fit(X, y), X


@pytest.fixture
def categorical_data():
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    X = np.column_stack(
        [rng.normal(size=45), np.tile([0.0, 1.0, 2.0], 15), rng.normal(size=45)]
    )
    y = 2.0 * X[:, 0] + X[:, 1]
    return LinearRegression().fit(X, y), X


def test_regression_average_defaults_and_display_attributes(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], grid_resolution=5
    )

    assert isinstance(display, PartialDependenceDisplay)
    assert display.features == [(0,)]
    assert display.feature_names == ["x0", "x1", "x2"]
    assert display.target_idx == 0
    assert display.kind == "average"
    assert display.subsample == 1000
    assert display.random_state is None

    pd_result = display.pd_results[0]
    assert set(pd_result.keys()) == {"grid_values", "average"}
    assert pd_result.average.shape == (1, 5)
    assert pd_result.grid_values[0].shape == (5,)
    assert np.all(np.diff(pd_result.grid_values[0]) > 0)

    assert set(display.deciles) == {0}
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.deciles[0], np.nanquantile(X[:, 0], np.arange(0.1, 1.0, 0.1))
    )

    assert display.axes_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.lines_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.contours_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.bars_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.heatmaps_.shape == (1, 1)

    ax = display.axes_[0, 0]
    line = display.lines_[0, 0]
    assert line is not None
    assert line.axes is ax
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_xdata(), pd_result.grid_values[0])
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_ydata(), pd_result.average[0])
    assert ax.get_xlabel() == "x0"
    assert ax.get_ylabel() == "Partial dependence"
    assert display.bounding_ax_ is not None
    assert display.figure_ is display.bounding_ax_.figure


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "features, feature_names, expected_index, expected_label",
    [
        (2, None, 2, "x2"),
        ("second", ["first", "second", "third"], 1, "second"),
    ],
)
def test_scalar_features_are_converted_to_one_way_tuples(
    regression_data, features, feature_names, expected_index, expected_label
):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        features,
        feature_names=feature_names,
        grid_resolution=4,
    )

    assert display.features == [(expected_index,)]
    assert display.axes_[0, 0].get_xlabel() == expected_label
    assert display.lines_[0, 0] is not None


def test_custom_values_override_grid_resolution_and_percentiles(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    custom_grid = np.array([-2.5, -0.25, 0.0, 4.0])

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=2,
        percentiles=(0.4, 0.6),
        custom_values={0: custom_grid},
    )

    np.testing.assert_array_equal(display.pd_results[0].grid_values[0], custom_grid)
    assert display.pd_results[0].average.shape == (1, custom_grid.size)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(display.lines_[0, 0].get_xdata(), custom_grid)


def test_dataframe_columns_are_used_as_feature_names(regression_data):
    pd = pytest.importorskip("pandas")
    estimator, X = regression_data
    dataframe = pd.DataFrame(X, columns=["alpha", "beta", "gamma"])

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, dataframe, ["alpha", "gamma"], grid_resolution=4
    )

    assert display.feature_names == ["alpha", "beta", "gamma"]
    assert display.features == [(0,), (2,)]
    assert display.axes_[0, 0].get_xlabel() == "alpha"
    assert display.axes_[0, 1].get_xlabel() == "gamma"


def test_two_way_average_creates_contour_and_decile_artists(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [(0, 1)], grid_resolution=4
    )

    assert display.features == [(0, 1)]
    pd_result = display.pd_results[0]
    assert len(pd_result.grid_values) == 2
    assert pd_result.average.shape == (1, 4, 4)
    assert display.contours_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.deciles_vlines_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.deciles_hlines_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.bars_[0, 0] is None
    assert set(display.deciles) == {0, 1}
    assert display.axes_[0, 0].get_xlabel() == "x0"
    assert display.axes_[0, 0].get_ylabel() == "x1"


def test_individual_kind_subsamples_ice_lines(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=5,
        kind="individual",
        subsample=4,
        random_state=0,
    )

    pd_result = display.pd_results[0]
    assert set(pd_result.keys()) == {"grid_values", "individual"}
    assert pd_result.individual.shape == (1, len(X), 5)
    assert display.kind == "individual"
    assert display.lines_.shape == (1, 1, 4)

    individual_rows = pd_result.individual[0]
    plotted_lines = display.lines_[0, 0]
    for line in plotted_lines:
        assert line is not None
        assert any(np.array_equal(line.get_ydata(), row) for row in individual_rows)


def test_both_kind_plots_average_after_subsampled_ice_lines(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=5,
        kind="both",
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
    )

    pd_result = display.pd_results[0]
    assert set(pd_result.keys()) == {"grid_values", "average", "individual"}
    assert display.kind == "both"
    assert display.lines_.shape == (1, 1, 4)

    average_line = display.lines_[0, 0, -1]
    assert average_line.get_label() == "average"
    np.testing.assert_allclose(average_line.get_ydata(), pd_result.average[0])

    individual_rows = pd_result.individual[0]
    for line in display.lines_[0, 0, :-1]:
        assert line is not None
        assert any(np.array_equal(line.get_ydata(), row) for row in individual_rows)


def test_list_kind_is_applied_per_feature(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    kinds = ["average", "individual"]

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0, 1],
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind=kinds,
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
    )

    assert display.kind == kinds
    assert set(display.pd_results[0].keys()) == {"grid_values", "average"}
    assert set(display.pd_results[1].keys()) == {"grid_values", "individual"}
    assert display.lines_.shape == (1, 2, 3)
    assert sum(line is not None for line in display.lines_.ravel()) == 4


def test_centered_plot_starts_at_zero(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    average_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], grid_resolution=4, centered=True
    )
    assert average_display.lines_[0, 0].get_ydata()[0] == pytest.approx(0.0)

    both_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind="both",
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
        centered=True,
    )
    for line in both_display.lines_[0, 0]:
        assert line.get_ydata()[0] == pytest.approx(0.0)


def test_sample_weight_is_used_for_average_dependence(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    grid = np.array([-2.0, 0.0, 2.0])
    sample_weight = np.zeros(len(X))
    sample_weight[0] = 1.0

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        sample_weight=sample_weight,
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )

    # With all weight on the first sample, each prediction only changes the
    # targeted feature; the complement features come from X[0].
    X_eval = np.tile(X[0], (grid.size, 1))
    X_eval[:, 0] = grid
    expected_average = estimator.predict(X_eval)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_average, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12
    )


def test_sample_weight_does_not_change_individual_predictions(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    sample_weight = np.arange(1.0, len(X) + 1.0)

    unweighted = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind="individual",
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
    )
    weighted = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        sample_weight=sample_weight,
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind="individual",
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        weighted.pd_results[0].individual, unweighted.pd_results[0].individual
    )


def test_binary_classification_response_methods():
    X, y = make_classification(
        n_samples=60,
        n_features=3,
        n_informative=2,
        n_redundant=0,
        random_state=0,
    )
    estimator = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, y)
    grid = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0])

    decision_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        response_method="decision_function",
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )
    assert decision_display.target_idx == 0
    expected_decision = []
    for value in grid:
        X_eval = X.copy()
        X_eval[:, 0] = value
        expected_decision.append(estimator.decision_function(X_eval).mean())
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        decision_display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_decision
    )

    proba_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        response_method="predict_proba",
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )
    expected_proba = []
    for value in grid:
        X_eval = X.copy()
        X_eval[:, 0] = value
        expected_proba.append(estimator.predict_proba(X_eval)[:, 1].mean())
    np.testing.assert_allclose(proba_display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_proba)
    assert np.all((proba_display.pd_results[0].average >= 0.0) & (
        proba_display.pd_results[0].average <= 1.0
    ))


def test_multiclass_requires_target_and_uses_requested_class():
    X, y = make_classification(
        n_samples=60,
        n_features=4,
        n_informative=3,
        n_redundant=0,
        n_classes=3,
        n_clusters_per_class=1,
        random_state=0,
    )
    estimator = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, y)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="target must be specified for multi-class"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(estimator, X, [0], grid_resolution=4)

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], target=2, grid_resolution=4
    )
    assert display.target_idx == 2
    assert display.pd_results[0].average.shape == (3, 4)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.lines_[0, 0].get_ydata(), display.pd_results[0].average[2]
    )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="target not in est.classes_"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [0], target=99, grid_resolution=4
        )


def test_multioutput_regression_requires_and_uses_target():
    X, y = make_regression(
        n_samples=40, n_features=3, n_targets=2, random_state=0
    )
    estimator = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError, match="target must be specified for multi-output regressors"
    ):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(estimator, X, [0], grid_resolution=4)

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], target=1, grid_resolution=4
    )
    assert display.target_idx == 1
    assert display.pd_results[0].average.shape == (2, 4)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.lines_[0, 0].get_ydata(), display.pd_results[0].average[1]
    )

    for invalid_target in (-1, 3):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="target must be in"):
            PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
                estimator, X, [0], target=invalid_target, grid_resolution=4
            )


def test_recursion_method_for_supported_tree_estimator(regression_data):
    _, X = regression_data
    y = X[:, 0] - X[:, 1] + 2.0 * X[:, 2]
    estimator = RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=5, random_state=0).fit(X, y)

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], method="recursion", grid_resolution=4
    )

    assert display.pd_results[0].average.shape == (1, 4)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(display.pd_results[0].average))

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="only applies when 'kind' is set to 'average'"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [0],
            method="recursion",
            kind="individual",
            grid_resolution=4,
        )


def test_feature_and_kind_validation_errors(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="as many elements as `features`"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [0, 1], kind=["average"], grid_resolution=4
        )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="iterable of size at most 2"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [(0, 1, 2)], grid_resolution=4
        )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="All entries of features must be less than"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(estimator, X, [3], grid_resolution=4)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="all features must be in"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(estimator, X, [-1], grid_resolution=4)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Feature 'missing' not in feature_names"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            ["missing"],
            feature_names=["a", "b", "c"],
            grid_resolution=4,
        )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="feature_names should not contain duplicates"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [0],
            feature_names=["same", "same", "other"],
            grid_resolution=4,
        )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="ICE plot cannot be rendered for 2-way"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [0, (0, 1)],
            kind=["average", "both"],
            grid_resolution=4,
        )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "subsample, message",
    [
        (0, "should be positive"),
        (-2, "should be positive"),
        (0.0, "should be in the \\(0, 1\\) range"),
        (1.0, "should be in the \\(0, 1\\) range"),
        (1.5, "should be in the \\(0, 1\\) range"),
    ],
)
def test_subsample_validation(regression_data, subsample, message):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=message):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [0], subsample=subsample, grid_resolution=4
        )


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "categorical_features, features, feature_names",
    [
        ([1], [1], None),
        ([False, True, False], [1], None),
        (["cat"], ["cat"], ["cont", "cat", "other"]),
    ],
)
def test_categorical_feature_specifications_create_bars(
    categorical_data, categorical_features, features, feature_names
):
    estimator, X = categorical_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        features,
        categorical_features=categorical_features,
        feature_names=feature_names,
        grid_resolution=3,
    )

    assert display.features == [(1,)]
    assert bool(display.is_categorical[0][0]) is True
    assert display.deciles == {}
    assert display.bars_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.lines_[0, 0] is None

    bar_container = display.bars_[0, 0]
    grid_values = display.pd_results[0].grid_values[0]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        [rectangle.get_height() for rectangle in bar_container],
        display.pd_results[0].average[0],
    )
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        [rectangle.get_x() + rectangle.get_width() / 2 for rectangle in bar_container],
        grid_values,
    )
    visible_tick_labels = [
        label for label in display.axes_[0, 0].get_xticklabels() if label.get_text()
    ]
    assert visible_tick_labels
    assert all(label.get_rotation() == pytest.approx(90.0) for label in visible_tick_labels)


def test_two_way_categorical_features_create_heatmap(categorical_data):
    estimator, _ = categorical_data
    first = np.repeat([0.0, 1.0, 2.0], 15)
    second = np.tile(np.repeat([10.0, 20.0, 30.0], 5), 3)
    X = np.column_stack([first, second])
    y = first + second
    estimator = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [(0, 1)],
        categorical_features=[0, 1],
        grid_resolution=3,
    )

    assert display.features == [(0, 1)]
    assert display.is_categorical == [(True, True)]
    assert display.deciles == {}
    assert display.heatmaps_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.bars_[0, 0] is None
    assert display.contours_[0, 0] is None
    assert display.heatmaps_[0, 0].get_array().shape == (3, 3)


def test_categorical_feature_validation_errors(categorical_data):
    estimator, X = categorical_data

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="array should be of shape \\(n_features,\\)"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [1],
            categorical_features=[True, False],
            grid_resolution=3,
        )

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError, match="Expected `categorical_features` to be an array-like"
    ):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [1],
            categorical_features=[1.0],
            grid_resolution=3,
        )

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError, match="pairs of continuous and categorical features"
    ):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [(0, 1)],
            categorical_features=[1],
            grid_resolution=3,
        )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="resolution of the computed grid is less"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [1],
            categorical_features=[1],
            grid_resolution=2,
        )

    with pytest.raises(
        ValueError, match="not possible to display individual effects for categorical"
    ):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator,
            X,
            [1],
            categorical_features=[1],
            kind="individual",
            grid_resolution=3,
        )


def test_style_keywords_override_defaults(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=4,
        line_kw={"color": "green", "linewidth": 4},
        pd_line_kw={"color": "red"},
    )
    line = display.lines_[0, 0]
    assert line.get_color() == "red"
    assert line.get_linewidth() == pytest.approx(4.0)

    contour_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [(0, 1)],
        grid_resolution=4,
        contour_kw={"alpha": 0.2},
    )
    assert contour_display.contours_[0, 0].get_alpha() == pytest.approx(0.2)


def test_individual_ice_style_keywords_override_line_kw(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind="individual",
        subsample=2,
        random_state=0,
        line_kw={"color": "green", "linewidth": 4},
        ice_lines_kw={"color": "purple", "linewidth": 2},
    )

    for line in display.lines_[0, 0]:
        assert line.get_color() == "purple"
        assert line.get_linewidth() == pytest.approx(2.0)


def test_explicit_array_of_axes_is_used_directly(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2)

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0, 1], ax=axes, grid_resolution=4
    )

    assert display.bounding_ax_ is None
    assert display.figure_ is fig
    assert display.axes_.shape == (2,)
    assert display.axes_[0] is axes[0]
    assert display.axes_[1] is axes[1]
    assert display.lines_.shape == (2,)
    assert display.lines_[0].axes is axes[0]
    assert display.lines_[1].axes is axes[1]


def test_explicit_axes_count_is_validated(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    _, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Expected ax to have 2 axes, got 3"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [0, 1], ax=axes, grid_resolution=4
        )


def test_single_bounding_axis_controls_grid_layout(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    fig, bounding_ax = plt.subplots()

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0, 1, 2],
        ax=bounding_ax,
        n_cols=2,
        grid_resolution=4,
    )

    assert display.bounding_ax_ is bounding_ax
    assert display.figure_ is fig
    assert display.axes_.shape == (2, 2)
    assert display.lines_.shape == (2, 2)
    assert not bounding_ax.axison
    assert display.lines_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.lines_[0, 1] is not None
    assert display.lines_[1, 0] is not None
    assert display.lines_[1, 1] is None

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="already used in another plot"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [0], ax=bounding_ax, grid_resolution=4
        )

def test_regression_average_defaults_and_display_attributes(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], grid_resolution=5
    )

    assert isinstance(display, PartialDependenceDisplay)
    assert display.features == [(0,)]
    assert display.feature_names == ["x0", "x1", "x2"]
    assert display.target_idx == 0
    assert display.kind == "average"
    assert display.subsample == 1000
    assert display.random_state is None

    pd_result = display.pd_results[0]
    assert set(pd_result.keys()) == {"grid_values", "average"}
    assert pd_result.average.shape == (1, 5)
    assert pd_result.grid_values[0].shape == (5,)
    assert np.all(np.diff(pd_result.grid_values[0]) > 0)

    assert set(display.deciles) == {0}
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.deciles[0], np.nanquantile(X[:, 0], np.arange(0.1, 1.0, 0.1))
    )

    assert display.axes_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.lines_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.contours_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.bars_.shape == (1, 1)
    assert display.heatmaps_.shape == (1, 1)

    ax = display.axes_[0, 0]
    line = display.lines_[0, 0]
    assert line is not None
    assert line.axes is ax
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_xdata(), pd_result.grid_values[0])
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_ydata(), pd_result.average[0])
    assert ax.get_xlabel() == "x0"
    assert ax.get_ylabel() == "Partial dependence"
    assert display.bounding_ax_ is not None
    assert display.figure_ is display.bounding_ax_.figure

def test_sample_weight_is_used_for_average_dependence(regression_data):
    estimator, X = regression_data
    grid = np.array([-2.0, 0.0, 2.0])
    sample_weight = np.zeros(len(X))
    sample_weight[0] = 1.0

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        sample_weight=sample_weight,
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )

    # With all weight on the first sample, each prediction only changes the
    # targeted feature; the complement features come from X[0].
    X_eval = np.tile(X[0], (grid.size, 1))
    X_eval[:, 0] = grid
    expected_average = estimator.predict(X_eval)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_average, rtol=1e-12, atol=1e-12
    )

    estimator, X = regression_data
    sample_weight = np.arange(1.0, len(X) + 1.0)

    unweighted = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind="individual",
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
    )
    weighted = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        sample_weight=sample_weight,
        grid_resolution=4,
        kind="individual",
        subsample=3,
        random_state=0,
    )

    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        weighted.pd_results[0].individual, unweighted.pd_results[0].individual
    )


def test_binary_classification_response_methods():
    X, y = make_classification(
        n_samples=60,
        n_features=3,
        n_informative=2,
        n_redundant=0,
        random_state=0,
    )
    estimator = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, y)
    grid = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0])

    decision_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        response_method="decision_function",
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )
    assert decision_display.target_idx == 0
    expected_decision = []
    for value in grid:
        X_eval = X.copy()
        X_eval[:, 0] = value
        expected_decision.append(estimator.decision_function(X_eval).mean())
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        decision_display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_decision
    )

    proba_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        response_method="predict_proba",
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )
    expected_proba = []
    for value in grid:
        X_eval = X.copy()
        X_eval[:, 0] = value
        expected_proba.append(estimator.predict_proba(X_eval)[:, 1].mean())
    np.testing.assert_allclose(proba_display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_proba)
    assert np.all((proba_display.pd_results[0].average >= 0.0) & (
        proba_display.pd_results[0].average <= 1.0
    ))


def test_multiclass_requires_target_and_uses_requested_class():
    X, y = make_classification(
        n_samples=60,
        n_features=4,
        n_informative=3,
        n_redundant=0,
        n_classes=3,
        n_clusters_per_class=1,
        random_state=0,
    )
    estimator = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, y)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="target must be specified for multi-class"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(estimator, X, [0], grid_resolution=4)

    display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator, X, [0], target=2, grid_resolution=4
    )
    assert display.target_idx == 2
    assert display.pd_results[0].average.shape == (3, 4)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        display.lines_[0, 0].get_ydata(), display.pd_results[0].average[2]
    )

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="target not in est.classes_"):
        PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
            estimator, X, [0], target=99, grid_resolution=4
        )


def test_multioutput_regression_requires_and_uses_target():
    X, y = make_regression(
        n_samples=40, n_features=3, n_targets=2, random_state=0
    )
    estimator = LinearRegression().fit(X, y)

def test_recursion_method_for_supported_tree_estimator(regression_data):

def test_binary_classification_response_methods():
    X, y = make_classification(

        n_informative=2,
        n_redundant=0,

    )
    estimator = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000).fit(X, y)
    grid = np.array([-1.0, 0.0, 1.0])

    decision_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        response_method="decision_function",
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )
    assert decision_display.target_idx == 0
    expected_decision = []
    for value in grid:
        X_eval = X.copy()
        X_eval[:, 0] = value
        expected_decision.append(estimator.decision_function(X_eval).mean())
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        decision_display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_decision
    )

    proba_display = PartialDependenceDisplay.from_estimator(
        estimator,
        X,
        [0],
        response_method="predict_proba",
        custom_values={0: grid},
    )
    expected_proba = []
    for value in grid:
        X_eval = X.copy()
        X_eval[:, 0] = value
        expected_proba.append(estimator.predict_proba(X_eval)[:, 1].mean())
    np.testing.assert_allclose(proba_display.pd_results[0].average[0], expected_proba)
    assert np.all((proba_display.pd_results[0].average >= 0.0) & (

def plot(
        self,
        *,
        ax=None,
        n_cols=3,
        line_kw=None,
        ice_lines_kw=None,
        pd_line_kw=None,
        contour_kw=None,
        bar_kw=None,
        heatmap_kw=None,
        pdp_lim=None,
        centered=False,
    ):
        """Plot partial dependence plots.

        Parameters
        ----------
        ax : Matplotlib axes or array-like of Matplotlib axes, default=None
            - If a single axis is passed in, it is treated as a bounding axes
                and a grid of partial dependence plots will be drawn within
                these bounds. The `n_cols` parameter controls the number of
                columns in the grid.
            - If an array-like of axes are passed in, the partial dependence
                plots will be drawn directly into these axes.
            - If `None`, a figure and a bounding axes is created and treated
                as the single axes case.

        n_cols : int, default=3
            The maximum number of columns in the grid plot. Only active when
            `ax` is a single axes or `None`.

        line_kw : dict, default=None
            Dict with keywords passed to the `matplotlib.pyplot.plot` call.
            For one-way partial dependence plots.

        ice_lines_kw : dict, default=None
            Dictionary with keywords passed to the `matplotlib.pyplot.plot` call.
            For ICE lines in the one-way partial dependence plots.
            The key value pairs defined in `ice_lines_kw` takes priority over
            `line_kw`.

            .. versionadded:: 1.0

        pd_line_kw : dict, default=None
            Dictionary with keywords passed to the `matplotlib.pyplot.plot` call.
            For partial dependence in one-way partial dependence plots.
            The key value pairs defined in `pd_line_kw` takes priority over
            `line_kw`.

            .. versionadded:: 1.0

        contour_kw : dict, default=None
            Dict with keywords passed to the `matplotlib.pyplot.contourf`
            call for two-way partial dependence plots.

        bar_kw : dict, default=None
            Dict with keywords passed to the `matplotlib.pyplot.bar`
            call for one-way categorical partial dependence plots.

            .. versionadded:: 1.2

        heatmap_kw : dict, default=None
            Dict with keywords passed to the `matplotlib.pyplot.imshow`
            call for two-way categorical partial dependence plots.

            .. versionadded:: 1.2

        pdp_lim : dict, default=None
            Global min and max average predictions, such that all plots will have the
            same scale and y limits. `pdp_lim[1]` is the global min and max for single
            partial dependence curves. `pdp_lim[2]` is the global min and max for
            two-way partial dependence curves. If `None` (default), the limit will be
            inferred from the global minimum and maximum of all predictions.

            .. versionadded:: 1.1

        centered : bool, default=False
            If `True`, the ICE and PD lines will start at the origin of the
            y-axis. By default, no centering is done.

            .. versionadded:: 1.1

        Returns
        -------
        display : :class:`~sklearn.inspection.PartialDependenceDisplay`
            Returns a :class:`~sklearn.inspection.PartialDependenceDisplay`
            object that contains the partial dependence plots.
        """

        check_matplotlib_support("plot_partial_dependence")
        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
        from matplotlib.gridspec import GridSpecFromSubplotSpec

        if isinstance(self.kind, str):
            kind = [self.kind] * len(self.features)
        else:
            kind = self.kind

        if self.is_categorical is None:
            is_categorical = [
                (False,) if len(fx) == 1 else (False, False) for fx in self.features
            ]
        else:
            is_categorical = self.is_categorical

        if len(kind) != len(self.features):
            raise ValueError(
                "When `kind` is provided as a list of strings, it should "
                "contain as many elements as `features`. `kind` contains "
                f"{len(kind)} element(s) and `features` contains "
                f"{len(self.features)} element(s)."
            )

        valid_kinds = {"average", "individual", "both"}
        if any([k not in valid_kinds for k in kind]):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Values provided to `kind` must be one of: {valid_kinds!r} or a list"
                f" of such values. Currently, kind={self.kind!r}"
            )

        # Center results before plotting
        if not centered:
            pd_results_ = self.pd_results
        else:
            pd_results_ = []
            for kind_plot, pd_result in zip(kind, self.pd_results):
                current_results = {"grid_values": pd_result["grid_values"]}

                if kind_plot in ("individual", "both"):
                    preds = pd_result.individual
                    preds = preds - preds[self.target_idx, :, 0, None]
                    current_results["individual"] = preds

                if kind_plot in ("average", "both"):
                    avg_preds = pd_result.average
                    avg_preds = avg_preds - avg_preds[self.target_idx, 0, None]
                    current_results["average"] = avg_preds

                pd_results_.append(Bunch(**current_results))

        if pdp_lim is None:
            # get global min and max average predictions of PD grouped by plot type
            pdp_lim = {}
            for kind_plot, pdp in zip(kind, pd_results_):
                values = pdp["grid_values"]
                preds = pdp.average if kind_plot == "average" else pdp.individual
                min_pd = preds[self.target_idx].min()
                max_pd = preds[self.target_idx].max()

                # expand the limits to account so that the plotted lines do not touch
                # the edges of the plot
                span = max_pd - min_pd
                min_pd -= 0.05 * span
                max_pd += 0.05 * span

                n_fx = len(values)
                old_min_pd, old_max_pd = pdp_lim.get(n_fx, (min_pd, max_pd))
                min_pd = min(min_pd, old_min_pd)
                max_pd = max(max_pd, old_max_pd)
                pdp_lim[n_fx] = (min_pd, max_pd)

        if line_kw is None:
            line_kw = {}
        if ice_lines_kw is None:
            ice_lines_kw = {}
        if pd_line_kw is None:
            pd_line_kw = {}
        if bar_kw is None:
            bar_kw = {}
        if heatmap_kw is None:
            heatmap_kw = {}

        if ax is None:
            _, ax = plt.subplots()

        if contour_kw is None:
            contour_kw = {}
        default_contour_kws = {"alpha": 0.75}
        contour_kw = _validate_style_kwargs(default_contour_kws, contour_kw)

        n_features = len(self.features)
        is_average_plot = [kind_plot == "average" for kind_plot in kind]
        if all(is_average_plot):
            # only average plots are requested
            n_ice_lines = 0
            n_lines = 1
        else:
            # we need to determine the number of ICE samples computed
            ice_plot_idx = is_average_plot.index(False)
            n_ice_lines = self._get_sample_count(
                len(pd_results_[ice_plot_idx].individual[0])
            )
            if any([kind_plot == "both" for kind_plot in kind]):
                n_lines = n_ice_lines + 1  # account for the average line
            else:
                n_lines = n_ice_lines

        if isinstance(ax, plt.Axes):
            # If ax was set off, it has most likely been set to off
            # by a previous call to plot.
            if not ax.axison:
                raise ValueError(
                    "The ax was already used in another plot "
                    "function, please set ax=display.axes_ "
                    "instead"
                )

            ax.set_axis_off()
            self.bounding_ax_ = ax
            self.figure_ = ax.figure

            n_cols = min(n_cols, n_features)
            n_rows = int(np.ceil(n_features / float(n_cols)))

            self.axes_ = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=object)
            if all(is_average_plot):
                self.lines_ = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=object)
            else:
                self.lines_ = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols, n_lines), dtype=object)
            self.contours_ = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=object)
            self.bars_ = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=object)
            self.heatmaps_ = np.empty((n_rows, n_cols), dtype=object)

            axes_ravel = self.axes_.ravel()

            gs = GridSpecFromSubplotSpec(
                n_rows, n_cols, subplot_spec=ax.get_subplotspec()
            )
            for i, spec in zip(range(n_features), gs):
                axes_ravel[i] = self.figure_.add_subplot(spec)

        else:  # array-like
            ax = np.asarray(ax, dtype=object)
            if ax.size != n_features:
                raise ValueError(
                    "Expected ax to have {} axes, got {}".format(n_features, ax.size)
                )

            if ax.ndim == 2:
                n_cols = ax.shape[1]
            else:
                n_cols = None

            self.bounding_ax_ = None
            self.figure_ = ax.ravel()[0].figure
            self.axes_ = ax
            if all(is_average_plot):
                self.lines_ = np.empty_like(ax, dtype=object)
            else:
                self.lines_ = np.empty(ax.shape + (n_lines,), dtype=object)
            self.contours_ = np.empty_like(ax, dtype=object)
            self.bars_ = np.empty_like(ax, dtype=object)
            self.heatmaps_ = np.empty_like(ax, dtype=object)

        # create contour levels for two-way plots
        if 2 in pdp_lim:
            Z_level = np.linspace(*pdp_lim[2], num=8)

        self.deciles_vlines_ = np.empty_like(self.axes_, dtype=object)
        self.deciles_hlines_ = np.empty_like(self.axes_, dtype=object)

        for pd_plot_idx, (axi, feature_idx, cat, pd_result, kind_plot) in enumerate(
            zip(
                self.axes_.ravel(),
                self.features,
                is_categorical,
                pd_results_,
                kind,
            )
        ):
            avg_preds = None
            preds = None
            feature_values = pd_result["grid_values"]
            if kind_plot == "individual":
                preds = pd_result.individual
            elif kind_plot == "average":
                avg_preds = pd_result.average
            else:  # kind_plot == 'both'
                avg_preds = pd_result.average
                preds = pd_result.individual

            if len(feature_values) == 1:
                # define the line-style for the current plot
                default_line_kws = {
                    "color": "C0",
                    "label": "average" if kind_plot == "both" else None,
                }
                if kind_plot == "individual":
                    default_ice_lines_kws = {"alpha": 0.3, "linewidth": 0.5}
                    default_pd_lines_kws = {}
                elif kind_plot == "both":
                    # by default, we need to distinguish the average line from
                    # the individual lines via color and line style
                    default_ice_lines_kws = {
                        "alpha": 0.3,
                        "linewidth": 0.5,
                        "color": "tab:blue",
                    }
                    default_pd_lines_kws = {
                        "color": "tab:orange",
                        "linestyle": "--",
                    }
                else:
                    default_ice_lines_kws = {}
                    default_pd_lines_kws = {}

                default_ice_lines_kws = {**default_line_kws, **default_ice_lines_kws}
                default_pd_lines_kws = {**default_line_kws, **default_pd_lines_kws}

                line_kw = _validate_style_kwargs(default_line_kws, line_kw)

                ice_lines_kw = _validate_style_kwargs(
                    _validate_style_kwargs(default_ice_lines_kws, line_kw), ice_lines_kw
                )
                del ice_lines_kw["label"]

                pd_line_kw = _validate_style_kwargs(
                    _validate_style_kwargs(default_pd_lines_kws, line_kw), pd_line_kw
                )

                default_bar_kws = {"color": "C0"}
                bar_kw = _validate_style_kwargs(default_bar_kws, bar_kw)

                default_heatmap_kw = {}
                heatmap_kw = _validate_style_kwargs(default_heatmap_kw, heatmap_kw)

                self._plot_one_way_partial_dependence(
                    kind_plot,
                    preds,
                    avg_preds,
                    feature_values[0],
                    feature_idx,
                    n_ice_lines,
                    axi,
                    n_cols,
                    pd_plot_idx,
                    n_lines,
                    ice_lines_kw,
                    pd_line_kw,
                    cat[0],
                    bar_kw,
                    pdp_lim,
                )
            else:
                self._plot_two_way_partial_dependence(
                    avg_preds,
                    feature_values,
                    feature_idx,
                    axi,
                    pd_plot_idx,
                    Z_level,
                    contour_kw,
                    cat[0] and cat[1],
                    heatmap_kw,
                )

        return self

        return n_samples

def _validate_style_kwargs(default_style_kwargs, user_style_kwargs):
    """Create valid style kwargs by avoiding Matplotlib alias errors.

    Matplotlib raises an error when, for example, 'color' and 'c', or 'linestyle' and
    'ls', are specified together. To avoid this, we automatically keep only the one
    specified by the user and raise an error if the user specifies both.

    Parameters
    ----------
    default_style_kwargs : dict
        The Matplotlib style kwargs used by default in the scikit-learn display.
    user_style_kwargs : dict
        The user-defined Matplotlib style kwargs.

    Returns
    -------
    valid_style_kwargs : dict
        The validated style kwargs taking into account both default and user-defined
        Matplotlib style kwargs.
    """

    invalid_to_valid_kw = {
        "ls": "linestyle",
        "c": "color",
        "ec": "edgecolor",
        "fc": "facecolor",

def _validate_style_kwargs(default_style_kwargs, user_style_kwargs):
    """Create valid style kwargs by avoiding Matplotlib alias errors.

    Matplotlib raises an error when, for example, 'color' and 'c', or 'linestyle' and
    'ls', are specified together. To avoid this, we automatically keep only the one
    specified by the user and raise an error if the user specifies both.

    Parameters
    ----------
    default_style_kwargs : dict
        The Matplotlib style kwargs used by default in the scikit-learn display.
    user_style_kwargs : dict
        The user-defined Matplotlib style kwargs.

    Returns
    -------
    valid_style_kwargs : dict
        The validated style kwargs taking into account both default and user-defined
        Matplotlib style kwargs.
    """

    invalid_to_valid_kw = {
        "ls": "linestyle",
        "c": "color",
        "ec": "edgecolor",
        "fc": "facecolor",
        "lw": "linewidth",
        "mec": "markeredgecolor",
        "mfcalt": "markerfacecoloralt",
        "ms": "markersize",
        "mew": "markeredgewidth",
        "mfc": "markerfacecolor",
        "aa": "antialiased",
        "ds": "drawstyle",
        "font": "fontproperties",
        "family": "fontfamily",
        "name": "fontname",
        "size": "fontsize",
        "stretch": "fontstretch",
        "style": "fontstyle",
        "variant": "fontvariant",
        "weight": "fontweight",
        "ha": "horizontalalignment",
        "va": "verticalalignment",
        "ma": "multialignment",
    }
    for invalid_key, valid_key in invalid_to_valid_kw.items():
        if invalid_key in user_style_kwargs and valid_key in user_style_kwargs:
            raise TypeError(
                f"Got both {invalid_key} and {valid_key}, which are aliases of one "
                "another"
            )
    valid_style_kwargs = default_style_kwargs.copy()

    for key in user_style_kwargs.keys():
        if key in invalid_to_valid_kw:
            valid_style_kwargs[invalid_to_valid_kw[key]] = user_style_kwargs[key]
        else:
            valid_style_kwargs[key] = user_style_kwargs[key]

    return valid_style_kwargs

"""Tests for PartialDependenceDisplay.plot."""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pytest
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.image import AxesImage

from sklearn.inspection import PartialDependenceDisplay
from sklearn.utils import Bunch


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def close_open_figures():
    yield

def make_pd_result(grid_values, average=None, individual=None):
    """Build the minimal result structure consumed by ``plot``."""
    result = {"grid_values": grid_values}
    if average is not None:
        result["average"] = np.asarray(average, dtype=float)
    if individual is not None:
        result["individual"] = np.asarray(individual, dtype=float)
    return Bunch(**result)


def make_display(
    pd_results,
    features,
    *,
    kind="average",
    feature_names=None,
    target_idx=0,
    deciles=None,
    is_categorical=None,
    subsample=1000,
    random_state=0,
):
    """Create a display without computing partial dependence."""
    if feature_names is None:
        feature_names = [f"feature_{idx}" for idx in range(len(features))]
    if deciles is None:
        deciles = {}
    return PartialDependenceDisplay(
        pd_results=pd_results,
        features=features,
        feature_names=feature_names,
        target_idx=target_idx,
        deciles=deciles,
        kind=kind,
        subsample=subsample,
        random_state=random_state,
        is_categorical=is_categorical,
    )


def test_plot_default_creates_figure_and_average_line():

    display = make_display(
        [make_pd_result([grid], average=average)],
        [(0,)],
        feature_names=["important feature"],
    )

    returned = display.plot()

    assert returned is display
    assert isinstance(display.bounding_ax_, plt.Axes)
    assert display.figure_ is display.bounding_ax_.figure
    assert display.axes_.shape == (1, 1)

    ax = display.axes_[0, 0]
    line = display.lines_[0, 0]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_xdata(), grid)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_ydata(), average[0])
    assert line.get_color() == "C0"
    assert ax.get_xlabel() == "important feature"
    assert ax.get_ylabel() == "Partial dependence"
    # The inferred limits are expanded by 5% of the prediction span on both sides.
    np.testing.assert_allclose(ax.get_ylim(), [0.8, 5.2])
    assert not display.bounding_ax_.axison

"""Tests for PartialDependenceDisplay.plot."""

import matplotlib

matplotlib.use("Agg")

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pytest
from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
from matplotlib.image import AxesImage
from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle

from sklearn.inspection import PartialDependenceDisplay
from sklearn.utils import Bunch


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def close_open_figures():
    yield
    plt.close("all")


def make_pd_result(grid_values, average=None, individual=None):
    """Build the minimal result structure consumed by ``plot``."""
    result = {"grid_values": grid_values}
    if average is not None:
        result["average"] = np.asarray(average, dtype=float)
    if individual is not None:
        result["individual"] = np.asarray(individual, dtype=float)
    return Bunch(**result)


def assert_rows_equal_unordered(actual, expected):
    """Compare samples without assuming the ICE subsampling order."""
    actual = np.asarray(actual)
    expected = np.asarray(expected)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(
        actual[np.lexsort(actual.T)], expected[np.lexsort(expected.T)]
    )


def make_display(
    pd_results,
    features,
    *,
    kind="average",
    feature_names=None,
    target_idx=0,
    deciles=None,
    is_categorical=None,
    subsample=1000,
    random_state=0,
):
    """Create a display without computing partial dependence."""
    if feature_names is None:
        feature_names = [f"feature_{idx}" for idx in range(len(features))]
    if deciles is None:
        deciles = {}
    return PartialDependenceDisplay(
        pd_results=pd_results,
        features=features,
        feature_names=feature_names,
        target_idx=target_idx,
        deciles=deciles,
        kind=kind,
        subsample=subsample,
        random_state=random_state,
        is_categorical=is_categorical,
    )


def test_plot_default_creates_figure_and_average_line():
    grid = np.array([0.0, 1.0, 2.0])
    average = np.array([[1.0, 3.0, 5.0]])
    display = make_display(
        [make_pd_result([grid], average=average)],
        [(0,)],
        feature_names=["important feature"],
    )

    returned = display.plot()

    assert returned is display
    assert isinstance(display.bounding_ax_, plt.Axes)
    assert display.figure_ is display.bounding_ax_.figure
    assert display.axes_.shape == (1, 1)

    ax = display.axes_[0, 0]
    line = display.lines_[0, 0]
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_xdata(), grid)
    np.testing.assert_allclose(line.get_ydata(), average[0])
    assert line.get_color() == "C0"
    assert ax.get_xlabel() == "important feature"
    assert ax.get_ylabel() == "Partial dependence"
    # The inferred limits are expanded by 5% of the prediction span on both sides.
    np.testing.assert_allclose(ax.get_ylim(), [0.8, 5.2])
    assert not display.bounding_ax_.axison


def test_plot_uses_requested_target_index():
    grid = np.array([0.0, 2.0, 4.0])
    average = np.array([[1.0, 2.0, 3.0], [10.0, 20.0, 30.0]])
    display = make_display(
        [make_pd_result([grid], average=average)],
        [(0,)],
        target_idx=1,
    )

    display.plot()

    np.testing.assert_allclose(display.lines_[0, 0].get_ydata(), average[1])


def test_plot_infers_global_y_limits_for_one_way_plots():
    grid = np.array([0.0, 1.0])
    first_average = np.array([[2.0, 4.0]])
    second_average = np.array([[10.0, 20.0]])
    display = make_display(
        [
            make_pd_result([grid], average=first_average),
            make_pd_result([grid], average=second_average),
        ],
        [(0,), (1,)],
    )

    display.plot()

    # Both curves are shown on a common scale, including the 5% padding.
    for ax in display.axes_.ravel():
        np.testing.assert_allclose(ax.get_ylim(), [1.9, 20.5])
    np.testing.assert_allclose(display.lines_[0, 0].get_ydata(), first_average[0])
    np.testing.assert_allclose(display.lines_[0, 1].get_ydata(), second_average[0])


def test_plot_uses_custom_pdp_limits():
    grid = np.array([0.0, 1.0])
    display = make_display(
        [make_pd_result([grid], average=np.array([[0.0, 1.0]]))],
        [(0,)],
    )

    display.plot(pdp_lim={1: (-7.0, 11.0)})

    np.testing.assert_allclose(display.axes_[0, 0].get_ylim(), [-7.0, 11.0])


def test_plot_creates_grid_with_requested_columns():
    grid = np.array([0.0, 1.0])
    results = [
        make_pd_result([grid], average=np.array([[value, value + 1.0]]))
        for value in (0.0, 2.0, 4.0)
    ]
    display = make_display(
        results,
        [(0,), (1,), (2,)],
        feature_names=["zero", "one", "two"],
    )

    display.plot(n_cols=2)

    assert display.axes_.shape == (2, 2)
    assert display.axes_[0, 0] is not None
    assert display.axes_[0, 1] is not None
    assert display.axes_[1, 0] is not None
    assert display.axes_[1, 1] is None
    assert [ax.get_xlabel() for ax in display.axes_.ravel()[:3]] == [
        "zero",
        "one",
        "two",
    ]
    assert display.axes_[0, 0].get_ylabel() == "Partial dependence"
    assert display.axes_[0, 1].get_ylabel() == ""
    assert display.axes_[1, 0].get_ylabel() == "Partial dependence"
    assert display.bounding_ax_ is display.figure_.axes[0]


def test_plot_accepts_array_of_axes():
    grid = np.array([0.0, 1.0])
    results = [
        make_pd_result([grid], average=np.array([[0.0, 1.0]])),
        make_pd_result([grid], average=np.array([[2.0, 3.0]])),
    ]
    display = make_display(results, [(0,), (1,)])
    _, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2)

    display.plot(ax=axes)

    assert display.bounding_ax_ is None

import pytest
import scipy.sparse as sp
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose, assert_array_equal

from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet, Lasso
from sklearn.utils._param_validation import InvalidParameterError


def make_data(n_samples=50, n_features=5, n_targets=None, noise=0.1, seed=0):
    """Return a small, well conditioned regression problem."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    coef = np.zeros(n_features)
    coef[: min(n_features, 3)] = np.array([1.5, 0.0, -2.0])[: min(n_features, 3)]
    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
    if n_targets is None:
        y = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
    else:
        Y = np.empty((n_samples, n_targets))
        for k in range(n_targets):
            Y[:, k] = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
        y = Y
    return X, y, coef

def test_fit_returns_self_and_populates_fitted_attributes():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1)
    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    assert model.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))
    assert np.ndim(model.intercept_) == 0
    assert np.isfinite(model.intercept_)
    # single target: n_iter_ and dual_gap_ are scalars, not sequences
    assert not isinstance(model.n_iter_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert not isinstance(model.dual_gap_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert 0 <= model.n_iter_ <= model.max_iter
    assert np.isfinite(model.dual_gap_)
    assert model.dual_gap_ >= -1e-10


def test_fit_recovers_noiseless_coefficients():
    X, y, coef = make_data(n_samples=60, noise=0.0)

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=1e-3, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coef, atol=1e-3)
    assert_allclose(model.predict(X), y, atol=1e-3)


def test_fit_zeroes_out_irrelevant_features():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # Features 1 and 3 of the generating model carry no signal.
    assert model.coef_[1] == 0.0
    assert model.coef_[3] == 0.0
    assert model.coef_[0] != 0.0
    assert model.coef_[2] != 0.0


def test_fit_constant_feature_gets_zero_coefficient():
    X, y, _ = make_data(noise=0.0)
    X = np.hstack([X, np.full((X.shape[0], 1), 3.0)])

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # A constant column is fully explained by the intercept.
    assert_allclose(model.coef_[-1], 0.0, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_is_deterministic():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    first = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    second = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    refit = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    refit.fit(X, y)  # refitting the same instance must not accumulate state

    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, second.coef_)
    assert first.intercept_ == second.intercept_
    assert first.n_iter_ == second.n_iter_
    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, refit.coef_)
    assert first.n_iter_ == refit.n_iter_


def test_fit_dual_gap_decreases_with_tighter_tolerance():
    X, y, _ = make_data(n_samples=40, n_features=4, noise=1.0)

    loose = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-1).fit(X, y)
    tight = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert tight.dual_gap_ <= loose.dual_gap_ + 1e-12
    assert tight.dual_gap_ <= 1e-8
    assert tight.n_iter_ >= loose.n_iter_


def test_fit_accepts_array_like_inputs():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    from_list = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X.tolist(), list(y))
    from_array = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(from_list.coef_, from_array.coef_, rtol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(from_list.intercept_, from_array.intercept_, rtol=1e-10)


def test_fit_single_sample():
    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(np.array([[2.0]]), np.array([3.0]))

    assert model.coef_.shape == (1,)

def test_fit_l1_ratio_one_matches_lasso():
    X, y, _ = make_data(noise=0.5)

    lasso = Lasso(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)
    elastic = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, l1_ratio=1.0, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(elastic.coef_, lasso.coef_, atol=1e-6)
    assert_allclose(elastic.intercept_, lasso.intercept_, atol=1e-6)


def test_fit_positive_constrains_coefficients():
    rng = np.random.RandomState(1)
    X = rng.randn(40, 4)
    y = X @ np.array([1.5, -2.0, 0.5, 1.0])

    unconstrained = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    constrained = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10, positive=True).fit(X, y)

    assert np.all(constrained.coef_ >= 0.0)
    assert np.any(constrained.coef_ > 0.0)
    # The negative signal cannot be represented: the solution must differ.
    assert not np.allclose(unconstrained.coef_, constrained.coef_)


def test_fit_fit_intercept_false_sets_zero_intercept():

    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, 0.0)
    assert not np.allclose(model.coef_, with_intercept.coef_)


def test_fit_max_iter_reached_raises_convergence_warning():

def test_fit_precompute_equivalence():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    default = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    with_precompute = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, precompute=True).fit(X, y)
    with_gram = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, precompute=X.T @ X).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(with_precompute.coef_, default.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_precompute.intercept_, default.intercept_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_gram.coef_, default.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_gram.intercept_, default.intercept_, atol=1e-10)

def test_fit_multi_output_shapes_and_per_target_solutions():
    X, Y, _ = make_data(n_targets=3, noise=0.3)
    n_targets = Y.shape[1]

    multi = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, Y)

    assert multi.coef_.shape == (n_targets, X.shape[1])
    assert model_intercept_shape(multi.intercept_) == (n_targets,)
    assert isinstance(multi.n_iter_, list)
    assert len(multi.n_iter_) == n_targets
    assert np.asarray(multi.dual_gap_).shape == (n_targets,)

    for k in range(n_targets):
        single = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, Y[:, k])
        assert_allclose(multi.coef_[k], single.coef_, atol=1e-8)
        assert_allclose(multi.intercept_[k], single.intercept_, atol=1e-8)
        assert multi.n_iter_[k] == single.n_iter_
        assert_allclose(multi.dual_gap_[k], single.dual_gap_, atol=1e-10)


def model_intercept_shape(intercept):
    return np.asarray(intercept).shape


def test_fit_two_dimensional_single_target_is_squeezed():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    flat = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    column = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y[:, np.newaxis])

    # A single target is stored with the same 1-d layout whatever the input
    # shape of ``y``.
    assert column.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.ndim(column.n_iter_) == 0
    assert np.ndim(column.dual_gap_) == 0
    assert_allclose(column.coef_, flat.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(column.intercept_, np.ravel(flat.intercept_)[0], atol=1e-10)

    rescaled = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y, sample_weight=10.0 * sw)

    sw = np.zeros(X.shape[0])

def test_fit_warm_start_reuses_previous_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True).fit(X, y)
    coefficients = model.coef_.copy()
    intercept = model.intercept_
    assert model.n_iter_ > 0

    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    # Starting from the previous solution, coordinate descent stops at once.
    assert model.n_iter_ == 0
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coefficients, atol=1e-12)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, intercept, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_warm_start_uses_user_provided_coef():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    solution = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True)
    model.coef_ = solution.coef_.copy()

    model.fit(X, y)

    assert model.n_iter_ == 0
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, solution.coef_, atol=1e-12)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, solution.intercept_, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_warm_start_multi_output_second_call_converges_immediately():
    X, Y, _ = make_data(n_targets=2, noise=0.3)

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True).fit(X, Y)
    coefficients = model.coef_.copy()

    model.fit(X, Y)

    assert model.coef_.shape == coefficients.shape
    assert_array_equal(np.asarray(model.n_iter_), np.zeros(len(model.n_iter_)))
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coefficients, atol=1e-12)

"""Unit tests for :meth:`sklearn.linear_model.ElasticNet.fit`.

The tests below treat ``ElasticNet.fit`` as a black box described by its public
contract: it validates its inputs (unless ``check_input=False``), fits a
coordinate-descent solution, stores ``coef_``/``intercept_``/``dual_gap_``/
``n_iter_`` and returns ``self``.
"""

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest
import scipy.sparse as sp
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose, assert_array_equal

from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet, Lasso
from sklearn.utils._param_validation import InvalidParameterError


def make_data(n_samples=50, n_features=5, n_targets=None, noise=0.1, seed=0):
    """Return a small, well conditioned regression problem."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    coef = np.zeros(n_features)
    coef[: min(n_features, 3)] = np.array([1.5, 0.0, -2.0])[: min(n_features, 3)]
    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
    if n_targets is None:
        y = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
    else:
        Y = np.empty((n_samples, n_targets))
        for k in range(n_targets):
            Y[:, k] = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
        y = Y
    return X, y, coef


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normal behaviour
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_returns_self_and_populates_fitted_attributes():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1)
    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    assert model.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))
    assert np.ndim(model.intercept_) == 0
    assert np.isfinite(model.intercept_)
    # single target: n_iter_ and dual_gap_ are scalars, not sequences
    assert not isinstance(model.n_iter_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert not isinstance(model.dual_gap_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert 0 <= model.n_iter_ <= model.max_iter
    assert np.isfinite(model.dual_gap_)
    assert model.dual_gap_ >= -1e-10


def test_fit_recovers_noiseless_coefficients():
    X, y, coef = make_data(n_samples=60, noise=0.0)

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=1e-3, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coef, atol=1e-3)
    assert_allclose(model.predict(X), y, atol=1e-3)


def test_fit_zeroes_out_irrelevant_features():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # Features 1 and 3 of the generating model carry no signal.
    assert model.coef_[1] == 0.0
    assert model.coef_[3] == 0.0
    assert model.coef_[0] != 0.0
    assert model.coef_[2] != 0.0


def test_fit_constant_feature_gets_zero_coefficient():
    X, y, _ = make_data(noise=0.0)
    X = np.hstack([X, np.full((X.shape[0], 1), 3.0)])

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # A constant column is fully explained by the intercept.
    assert_allclose(model.coef_[-1], 0.0, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_is_deterministic():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    first = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    second = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    refit = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    refit.fit(X, y)  # refitting the same instance must not accumulate state

    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, second.coef_)
    assert first.intercept_ == second.intercept_
    assert first.n_iter_ == second.n_iter_
    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, refit.coef_)
    assert first.n_iter_ == refit.n_iter_


def test_fit_dual_gap_decreases_with_tighter_tolerance():
    X, y, _ = make_data(n_samples=40, n_features=4, noise=1.0)

    loose = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-1).fit(X, y)
    tight = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert tight.dual_gap_ <= loose.dual_gap_ + 1e-12
    assert tight.dual_gap_ <= 1e-8
    assert tight.n_iter_ >= loose.n_iter_


def test_fit_accepts_array_like_inputs():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    from_list = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X.tolist(), list(y))
    from_array = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(from_list.coef_, from_array.coef_, rtol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(from_list.intercept_, from_array.intercept_, rtol=1e-10)


def test_fit_single_sample():
    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(np.array([[2.0]]), np.array([3.0]))

    lasso = Lasso(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)
    elastic = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, l1_ratio=1.0, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(elastic.coef_, lasso.coef_, atol=1e-6)

def test_fit_positive_constrains_coefficients():
    rng = np.random.RandomState(1)
    X = rng.randn(40, 4)
    y = X @ np.array([1.5, -2.0, 0.5, 1.0])

    unconstrained = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    constrained = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10, positive=True).fit(X, y)

def test_fit_precompute_equivalence():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    default = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    with_precompute = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, precompute=True).fit(X, y)
    with_gram = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, precompute=X.T @ X).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(with_precompute.coef_, default.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_precompute.intercept_, default.intercept_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_gram.coef_, default.coef_, atol=1e-10)

def test_fit_multi_output_shapes_and_per_target_solutions():
    X, Y, _ = make_data(n_targets=3, noise=0.3)
    n_targets = Y.shape[1]

    assert multi.coef_.shape == (n_targets, X.shape[1])
    assert model_intercept_shape(multi.intercept_) == (n_targets,)
    assert isinstance(multi.n_iter_, list)

    assert np.asarray(multi.dual_gap_).shape == (n_targets,)

    for k in range(n_targets):

        assert_allclose(multi.coef_[k], single.coef_, atol=1e-8)
        assert_allclose(multi.intercept_[k], single.intercept_, atol=1e-8)
        assert multi.n_iter_[k] == single.n_iter_
        assert_allclose(multi.dual_gap_[k], single.dual_gap_, atol=1e-10)

"""Unit tests for :meth:`sklearn.linear_model.ElasticNet.fit`.

The tests below treat ``ElasticNet.fit`` as a black box described by its public
contract: it validates its inputs (unless ``check_input=False``), fits a
coordinate-descent solution, stores ``coef_``/``intercept_``/``dual_gap_``/

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest
import scipy.sparse as sp
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose, assert_array_equal

from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet, Lasso
from sklearn.utils._param_validation import InvalidParameterError


def make_data(n_samples=50, n_features=5, n_targets=None, noise=0.1, seed=0):
    """Return a small, well conditioned regression problem."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    coef = np.zeros(n_features)
    coef[: min(n_features, 3)] = np.array([1.5, 0.0, -2.0])[: min(n_features, 3)]
    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
    if n_targets is None:
        y = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
    else:
        Y = np.empty((n_samples, n_targets))
        for k in range(n_targets):
            Y[:, k] = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
        y = Y
    return X, y, coef

def test_fit_returns_self_and_populates_fitted_attributes():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1)
    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    assert model.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))
    assert np.ndim(model.intercept_) == 0
    assert np.isfinite(model.intercept_)
    # single target: n_iter_ and dual_gap_ are scalars, not sequences
    assert not isinstance(model.n_iter_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert not isinstance(model.dual_gap_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert 0 <= model.n_iter_ <= model.max_iter
    assert np.isfinite(model.dual_gap_)
    assert model.dual_gap_ >= -1e-10

    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coef, atol=1e-3)

def test_fit_is_deterministic():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    first = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    second = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    refit = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    refit.fit(X, y)  # refitting the same instance must not accumulate state

    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, second.coef_)
    assert first.intercept_ == second.intercept_
    assert first.n_iter_ == second.n_iter_
    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, refit.coef_)

def test_fit_multi_output_shapes_and_per_target_solutions():
    X, Y, _ = make_data(n_targets=3, noise=0.3)
    n_targets = Y.shape[1]

    multi = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, Y)

    assert multi.coef_.shape == (n_targets, X.shape[1])
    assert model_intercept_shape(multi.intercept_) == (n_targets,)
    assert isinstance(multi.n_iter_, list)
    assert len(multi.n_iter_) == n_targets
    assert np.asarray(multi.dual_gap_).shape == (n_targets,)

        assert_allclose(multi.coef_[k], single.coef_, atol=1e-8)
        assert_allclose(multi.intercept_[k], single.intercept_, atol=1e-8)
        assert multi.n_iter_[k] == single.n_iter_
        assert_allclose(multi.dual_gap_[k], single.dual_gap_, atol=1e-10)


def model_intercept_shape(intercept):

"""Unit tests for :meth:`sklearn.linear_model.ElasticNet.fit`.

The tests below treat ``ElasticNet.fit`` as a black box described by its public
contract: it validates its inputs (unless ``check_input=False``), fits a
coordinate-descent solution, stores ``coef_``/``intercept_``/``dual_gap_``/
``n_iter_`` and returns ``self``.
"""

import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest
import scipy.sparse as sp
from numpy.testing import assert_allclose, assert_array_equal

from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet, Lasso
from sklearn.utils._param_validation import InvalidParameterError


def make_data(n_samples=50, n_features=5, n_targets=None, noise=0.1, seed=0):
    """Return a small, well conditioned regression problem."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    coef = np.zeros(n_features)
    coef[: min(n_features, 3)] = np.array([1.5, 0.0, -2.0])[: min(n_features, 3)]
    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
    if n_targets is None:
        y = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
    else:
        Y = np.empty((n_samples, n_targets))
        for k in range(n_targets):
            Y[:, k] = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples)
        y = Y
    return X, y, coef


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Normal behaviour
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_returns_self_and_populates_fitted_attributes():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1)
    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    assert model.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))
    assert np.ndim(model.intercept_) == 0
    assert np.isfinite(model.intercept_)
    # single target: n_iter_ and dual_gap_ are scalars, not sequences
    assert not isinstance(model.n_iter_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert not isinstance(model.dual_gap_, (list, np.ndarray))
    assert 0 <= model.n_iter_ <= model.max_iter
    assert np.isfinite(model.dual_gap_)
    assert model.dual_gap_ >= -1e-10


def test_fit_recovers_noiseless_coefficients():
    X, y, coef = make_data(n_samples=60, noise=0.0)

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=1e-3, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coef, atol=1e-2)
    assert_allclose(model.predict(X), y, atol=1e-2)


def test_fit_zeroes_out_irrelevant_features():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # Features 1 and 3 of the generating model carry no signal.
    assert model.coef_[1] == 0.0
    assert model.coef_[3] == 0.0
    assert model.coef_[0] != 0.0
    assert model.coef_[2] != 0.0


def test_fit_constant_feature_gets_zero_coefficient():
    X, y, _ = make_data(noise=0.0)
    X = np.hstack([X, np.full((X.shape[0], 1), 3.0)])

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # A constant column is fully explained by the intercept.
    assert_allclose(model.coef_[-1], 0.0, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_huge_alpha_gives_all_zero_coefficients():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=1e6, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert_array_equal(model.coef_, np.zeros(X.shape[1]))
    # Everything is explained by the intercept, i.e. the mean of the target.
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, np.mean(y), atol=1e-6)

    no_intercept = ElasticNet(alpha=1e6, tol=1e-10, fit_intercept=False).fit(X, y)
    assert_array_equal(no_intercept.coef_, np.zeros(X.shape[1]))
    assert_allclose(no_intercept.intercept_, 0.0)


def test_fit_underdetermined_problem():
    rng = np.random.RandomState(2)
    X = rng.randn(6, 15)
    y = X @ rng.randn(15)

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert model.coef_.shape == (15,)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))
    assert np.isfinite(model.dual_gap_)


def test_fit_is_deterministic():
    X, y, _ = make_data()
