def test_fit_dual_gap_decreases_with_tighter_tolerance():
    X, y, _ = make_data(n_samples=40, n_features=4, noise=1.0)

    loose = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-1).fit(X, y)
    tight = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert tight.dual_gap_ <= loose.dual_gap_ + 1e-12
    assert tight.dual_gap_ <= 1e-8
    assert tight.n_iter_ >= loose.n_iter_


def test_fit_accepts_array_like_inputs():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    from_list = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X.tolist(), list(y))
    from_array = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(from_list.coef_, from_array.coef_, rtol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(from_list.intercept_, from_array.intercept_, rtol=1e-10)


def test_fit_single_sample():
    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(np.array([[2.0]]), np.array([3.0]))

    assert model.coef_.shape == (1,)
    assert model.coef_[0] == 0.0
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, 3.0)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# alpha / hyper-parameter effects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_alpha_zero_warns():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="With alpha=0, this algorithm does not converge"):
        model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.0, tol=1e-6).fit(X, y)

    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))


def test_fit_no_warning_for_positive_alpha():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", UserWarning)
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore", ConvergenceWarning)
        ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(X, y)


def test_fit_l1_ratio_one_matches_lasso():
    X, y, _ = make_data(noise=0.5)

    lasso = Lasso(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)
    elastic = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, l1_ratio=1.0, tol=1e-10, max_iter=10_000).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(elastic.coef_, lasso.coef_, atol=1e-6)
    assert_allclose(elastic.intercept_, lasso.intercept_, atol=1e-6)


def test_fit_positive_constrains_coefficients():
    rng = np.random.RandomState(1)
    X = rng.randn(40, 4)
    y = X @ np.array([1.5, -2.0, 0.5, 1.0])

    unconstrained = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    constrained = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10, positive=True).fit(X, y)

    assert np.all(constrained.coef_ >= 0.0)
    assert np.any(constrained.coef_ > 0.0)
    # The negative signal cannot be represented: the solution must differ.
    assert not np.allclose(unconstrained.coef_, constrained.coef_)


def test_fit_fit_intercept_false_sets_zero_intercept():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, fit_intercept=False).fit(X, y)
    with_intercept = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, 0.0)
    assert not np.allclose(model.coef_, with_intercept.coef_)


def test_fit_max_iter_reached_raises_convergence_warning():
    X, y, _ = make_data(n_samples=40, n_features=4, noise=2.0)

    with pytest.warns(ConvergenceWarning, match="Objective did not converge"):
        model = ElasticNet(alpha=1e-4, tol=1e-14, max_iter=1).fit(X, y)

    assert model.n_iter_ == 1


def test_fit_precompute_equivalence():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    default = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    with_precompute = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, precompute=True).fit(X, y)
    # The provided Gram matrix is ignored (and a warning emitted) because X is
    # centered when ``fit_intercept=True``.
    with pytest.warns(UserWarning, match="Gram matrix was provided"):
        with_gram = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, precompute=X.T @ X).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(with_precompute.coef_, default.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_precompute.intercept_, default.intercept_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_gram.coef_, default.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(with_gram.intercept_, default.intercept_, atol=1e-10)


def test_fit_selection_random_is_reproducible():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    first = ElasticNet(
        alpha=0.1, selection="random", random_state=0, tol=1e-10
    ).fit(X, y)
    second = ElasticNet(
        alpha=0.1, selection="random", random_state=0, tol=1e-10
    ).fit(X, y)

    assert_array_equal(first.coef_, second.coef_)
    assert first.n_iter_ == second.n_iter_

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_multi_output_shapes_and_per_target_solutions():
    X, Y, _ = make_data(n_targets=3, noise=0.3)
    n_targets = Y.shape[1]

    multi = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, Y)

    assert multi.coef_.shape == (n_targets, X.shape[1])
    assert np.asarray(multi.intercept_).shape == (n_targets,)
    assert isinstance(multi.n_iter_, list)
    assert len(multi.n_iter_) == n_targets
    assert np.asarray(multi.dual_gap_).shape == (n_targets,)

    for k in range(n_targets):
        single = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, Y[:, k])
        assert_allclose(multi.coef_[k], single.coef_, atol=1e-8)
        assert_allclose(multi.intercept_[k], single.intercept_, atol=1e-8)
        assert multi.n_iter_[k] == single.n_iter_
        assert_allclose(multi.dual_gap_[k], single.dual_gap_, atol=1e-10)


def test_fit_two_dimensional_single_target_is_squeezed():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    flat = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    column = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y[:, np.newaxis])

    # A single target is stored with the same 1-d layout whatever the input
    # shape of ``y``.
    assert column.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.ndim(column.n_iter_) == 0
    assert np.ndim(column.dual_gap_) == 0
    assert_allclose(column.coef_, flat.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(column.intercept_, np.ravel(flat.intercept_)[0], atol=1e-10)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_sample_weight_as_number_is_ignored():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    unweighted = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    weighted = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y, sample_weight=7.0)

    assert_array_equal(weighted.coef_, unweighted.coef_)
    assert weighted.intercept_ == unweighted.intercept_
    assert weighted.n_iter_ == unweighted.n_iter_


def test_fit_sample_weight_rescaling_invariance():
    X, y, _ = make_data()
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    sw = rng.rand(X.shape[0]) + 0.5

    reference = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sw)
    rescaled = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y, sample_weight=10.0 * sw)

    assert_allclose(rescaled.coef_, reference.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(rescaled.intercept_, reference.intercept_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(rescaled.dual_gap_, reference.dual_gap_, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_sample_weight_changes_the_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data(noise=1.0)
    unweighted = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    sw = np.zeros(X.shape[0])
    sw[: X.shape[0] // 5] = 1.0
    weighted = ElasticNet(alpha=0.05, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sw)

    assert not np.allclose(weighted.coef_, unweighted.coef_)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(weighted.coef_))
    assert np.isfinite(weighted.intercept_)


def test_fit_sample_weight_accepts_array_like():
    X, y, _ = make_data()
    sw = np.linspace(0.5, 2.0, X.shape[0])

    from_list = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y, sample_weight=list(sw))

    assert_allclose(from_list.coef_, from_array.coef_, atol=1e-10)

def test_fit_warm_start_reuses_previous_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True).fit(X, y)
    coefficients = model.coef_.copy()
    intercept = model.intercept_
    assert model.n_iter_ > 0

    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    # Starting from the previous solution, coordinate descent stops at once.
    assert model.n_iter_ == 0
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coefficients, atol=1e-12)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, intercept, atol=1e-12)

    solution = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True)
    model.coef_ = solution.coef_.copy()

    model.fit(X, y)

    assert model.n_iter_ == 0
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, solution.coef_, atol=1e-12)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, solution.intercept_, atol=1e-12)

    X_bad[0, 0] = np.inf

    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("ignore")
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="non-finite parameter"):
            ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(X_bad, y.astype(np.float64), check_input=False)


def test_fit_validated_path_rejects_non_finite_data():
    X, y, _ = make_data()
    X_bad = X.copy()
    X_bad[0, 0] = np.nan

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Input X contains NaN"):
        ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(X_bad, y)

    y_bad = y.copy()
    y_bad[0] = np.inf
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="Input y contains"):
        ElasticNet(alpha=0.1).fit(X, y_bad)

# copy_X side effects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_copy_X_true_leaves_input_untouched():
    X, y, _ = make_data()
    X_f = np.asfortranarray(X.astype(np.float64))
    X_original = X_f.copy()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, copy_X=True).fit(X_f, y)

    assert_array_equal(X_f, X_original)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(model.coef_))


def test_fit_copy_X_false_same_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data()
    reference = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, copy_X=True).fit(X, y)
    X_f = np.asfortranarray(X.astype(np.float64))

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, copy_X=False).fit(X_f, y)

    assert_allclose(model.coef_, reference.coef_, atol=1e-10)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, reference.intercept_, atol=1e-10)

# warm_start
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_fit_warm_start_reuses_previous_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True).fit(X, y)
    coefficients = model.coef_.copy()
    intercept = model.intercept_
    assert model.n_iter_ > 0

    returned = model.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is model
    # Starting from the previous solution, coordinate descent stops at once.
    assert model.n_iter_ == 0
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coefficients, atol=1e-12)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, intercept, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_warm_start_uses_user_provided_coef():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    solution = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True)
    model.coef_ = solution.coef_.copy()

    model.fit(X, y)

    assert model.n_iter_ == 0
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, solution.coef_, atol=1e-12)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, solution.intercept_, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_warm_start_multi_output_second_call_converges_immediately():
    X, Y, _ = make_data(n_targets=2, noise=0.3)

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True).fit(X, Y)
    coefficients = model.coef_.copy()

    model.fit(X, Y)

    assert model.coef_.shape == coefficients.shape
    assert_array_equal(np.asarray(model.n_iter_), np.zeros(len(model.n_iter_)))
    assert_allclose(model.coef_, coefficients, atol=1e-12)


def test_fit_warm_start_with_different_n_features_raises():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.1, warm_start=True).fit(X, y)

    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        model.fit(X[:, :-1], y)


def test_fit_without_warm_start_discards_previous_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.5, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)
    strongly_regularized = model.coef_.copy()

    model.set_params(alpha=0.01)
    model.fit(X, y)
    fresh = ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    # The previous coefficients are not reused: the result is bit-for-bit the
    # one obtained by an estimator that was never fitted before.
    assert not np.allclose(model.coef_, strongly_regularized)
    assert_array_equal(model.coef_, fresh.coef_)
    assert model.n_iter_ == fresh.n_iter_


def test_fit_warm_start_with_new_alpha_converges_to_cold_solution():
    X, y, _ = make_data()

    model = ElasticNet(alpha=0.5, tol=1e-10, warm_start=True).fit(X, y)
    model.set_params(alpha=0.01)
    model.fit(X, y)

    cold = ElasticNet(alpha=0.01, tol=1e-10).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(model.coef_, cold.coef_, atol=1e-8)
    assert_allclose(model.intercept_, cold.intercept_, atol=1e-8)

@_fit_context(prefer_skip_nested_validation=True)
    def fit(self, X, y, sample_weight=None, **params):
        """Fit model with internal cross-validation and with coordinate descent.

        Fit is on grid of alphas and best alpha estimated by cross-validation.

        Parameters
        ----------
        X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
            Training data. If y is mono-output,
            X can be sparse. Note that large sparse matrices and arrays
            requiring `int64` indices are not accepted.

        y : array-like of shape (n_samples,) or (n_samples, n_targets)
            Target values.

        sample_weight : float or array-like of shape (n_samples,), \
                default=None
            Sample weights used for fitting and evaluation of the weighted
            mean squared error of each cv-fold. Note that the cross validated
            MSE that is finally used to find the best model is the unweighted
            mean over the (weighted) MSEs of each test fold.

        **params : dict, default=None
            Parameters to be passed to the CV splitter.

            .. versionadded:: 1.4
                Only available if `enable_metadata_routing=True`,
                which can be set by using
                ``sklearn.set_config(enable_metadata_routing=True)``.
                See :ref:`Metadata Routing User Guide <metadata_routing>` for
                more details.

        Returns
        -------
        self : object
            Returns an instance of fitted model.
        """
        _raise_for_params(params, self, "fit")

        # This makes sure that there is no duplication in memory.
        # Dealing right with copy_X is important in the following:
        # Multiple functions touch X and subsamples of X and can induce a
        # lot of duplication of memory.
        # There is no need copy X if the model is fit without an intercept.
        copy_X = self.copy_X and self.fit_intercept  # TODO: Sample_weights?

        check_y_params = dict(
            copy=False, dtype=[np.float64, np.float32], ensure_2d=False
        )
        if isinstance(X, np.ndarray) or sparse.issparse(X):
            # Keep a reference to X
            reference_to_old_X = X
            # Let us not impose Fortran-contiguity so far: In the cross-validation
            # loop, rows of X will be subsampled and produce non-F-contiguous X_fold
            # anyway. _path_residual will take care about it.

            # Need to validate separately here.
            # We can't pass multi_output=True because that would allow y to be
            # csr. We also want to allow y to be 64 or 32 but check_X_y only
            # allows to convert for 64.
            check_X_params = dict(
                accept_sparse="csr",
                dtype=[np.float64, np.float32],
                force_writeable=True,
                copy=False,
                accept_large_sparse=False,
            )
            X, y = validate_data(
                self, X, y, validate_separately=(check_X_params, check_y_params)
            )
            if sparse.issparse(X):
                if hasattr(reference_to_old_X, "data") and not np.may_share_memory(

                    copy_X = False
            elif not np.may_share_memory(reference_to_old_X, X):

                copy_X = False

        else:

            # We can't pass multi_output=True because that would allow y to be
            # csr. We also want to allow y to be 64 or 32 but check_X_y only

            check_X_params = dict(
                accept_sparse="csr",
                dtype=[np.float64, np.float32],
                order=None,
                force_writeable=True,
                copy=copy_X,
            )
            X, y = validate_data(
                self, X, y, validate_separately=(check_X_params, check_y_params)
            )

        check_consistent_length(X, y)

            if y.ndim > 1 and y.shape[1] > 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    "For multi-task outputs, use MultiTask%s" % self.__class__.__name__
                )
            y = column_or_1d(y, warn=True)
        else:
            if y.ndim == 1:
                raise ValueError(
                    "For mono-task outputs, use %sCV" % self.__class__.__name__[9:]
                )

        if isinstance(sample_weight, numbers.Number):
            sample_weight = None
        if sample_weight is not None:

        model = self._get_estimator()

        # All LinearModelCV parameters except 'cv' are acceptable
        path_params = self.get_params()

        # fit_intercept is not a parameter of the path function
        path_params.pop("fit_intercept", None)

        if "l1_ratio" in path_params:
            l1_ratios = np.atleast_1d(path_params["l1_ratio"])
            # For the first path, we need to set l1_ratio
            path_params["l1_ratio"] = l1_ratios[0]
        else:
            l1_ratios = [
                1,
            ]
        path_params.pop("cv", None)
        path_params.pop("n_jobs", None)

        n_l1_ratio = len(l1_ratios)

        check_scalar_alpha = partial(
            check_scalar,
            target_type=Real,
            min_val=0.0,
            include_boundaries="left",
        )

        if isinstance(self.alphas, Integral):
            alphas = [
                _alpha_grid(
                    X,
                    y,
                    l1_ratio=l1_ratio,
                    fit_intercept=self.fit_intercept,
                    # Note: MultiTaskElasticNetCV has no attribute 'positive'
                    positive=getattr(self, "positive", False),
                    eps=self.eps,
                    n_alphas=self.alphas,
                    sample_weight=sample_weight,
                )
                for l1_ratio in l1_ratios
            ]
        else:
            # Making sure alphas entries are scalars.
            for index, alpha in enumerate(self.alphas):
                check_scalar_alpha(alpha, f"alphas[{index}]")
            # Making sure alphas is properly ordered.
            alphas = np.tile(np.sort(self.alphas)[::-1], (n_l1_ratio, 1))

        path_params["copy_X"] = copy_X
        # We are not computing in parallel, we can modify X
        # inplace in the folds
        if effective_n_jobs(self.n_jobs) > 1:
            path_params["copy_X"] = False

        # init cross-validation generator
        cv = check_cv(self.cv)

        if _routing_enabled():
            routed_params = process_routing(
                self,
                "fit",
                sample_weight=sample_weight,
                **params,
            )
        else:
            routed_params = _manual_routing({"splitter": {}})

        # Compute path for all folds and compute MSE to get the best alpha
        folds = list(cv.split(X, y, **routed_params.splitter.split))
        best_mse = np.inf

        # We do a double for loop folded in one, in order to be able to
        # iterate in parallel on l1_ratio and folds
        jobs = (
            delayed(_path_residuals)(
                X,
                y,
                sample_weight,
                train,
                test,
                self.fit_intercept,
                self.path,
                path_params,
                alphas=this_alphas,
                l1_ratio=this_l1_ratio,
                dtype=X.dtype.type,
            )
            for this_l1_ratio, this_alphas in zip(l1_ratios, alphas)
            for train, test in folds
        )
        mse_paths = Parallel(
            n_jobs=self.n_jobs,
            verbose=self.verbose,
            prefer="threads",
        )(jobs)
        mse_paths = np.reshape(mse_paths, (n_l1_ratio, len(folds), -1))
        # The mean is computed over folds.
        mean_mse = np.mean(mse_paths, axis=1)
        self.mse_path_ = np.squeeze(np.moveaxis(mse_paths, 2, 1))
        for l1_ratio, l1_alphas, mse_alphas in zip(l1_ratios, alphas, mean_mse):
            i_best_alpha = np.argmin(mse_alphas)
            this_best_mse = mse_alphas[i_best_alpha]
            if this_best_mse < best_mse:
                best_alpha = l1_alphas[i_best_alpha]
                best_l1_ratio = l1_ratio
                best_mse = this_best_mse

        self.l1_ratio_ = best_l1_ratio
        self.alpha_ = best_alpha
        if isinstance(self.alphas, Integral):
            self.alphas_ = np.asarray(alphas)
            if n_l1_ratio == 1:
                self.alphas_ = self.alphas_[0]
        # Remove duplicate alphas in case alphas is provided.
        else:
            self.alphas_ = np.asarray(alphas[0])

        # Refit the model with the parameters selected
        X, y = _set_order(X, y, order="F")
        common_params = {
            name: value
            for name, value in self.get_params().items()
            if name in model.get_params()
        }
        model.set_params(**common_params)
        model.alpha = best_alpha
        model.l1_ratio = best_l1_ratio
        model.copy_X = copy_X
        precompute = getattr(self, "precompute", None)
        if isinstance(precompute, str) and precompute == "auto":
            model.precompute = False

        if sample_weight is None:
            # MultiTaskElasticNetCV does not (yet) support sample_weight, even
            # not sample_weight=None.
            model.fit(X, y)
        else:
            model.fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)
        if not hasattr(self, "l1_ratio"):
            del self.l1_ratio_
        self.coef_ = model.coef_
        self.intercept_ = model.intercept_
        self.dual_gap_ = model.dual_gap_
        self.n_iter_ = model.n_iter_

def _raise_for_params(params, owner, method, allow=None):
    """Raise an error if metadata routing is not enabled and params are passed.

    .. versionadded:: 1.4

    Parameters
    ----------
    params : dict
        The metadata passed to a method.

    owner : object
        The object to which the method belongs.

    method : str
        The name of the method, e.g. "fit".

    allow : list of str, default=None
        A list of parameters which are allowed to be passed even if metadata
        routing is not enabled.

    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If metadata routing is not enabled and params are passed.
    """
    caller = f"{_routing_repr(owner)}.{method}" if method else _routing_repr(owner)

    allow = allow if allow is not None else {}

    if not _routing_enabled() and (params.keys() - allow):

            " `sklearn.set_config`. See the User Guide"
            " <https://scikit-learn.org/stable/metadata_routing.html> for more"

"""Tests for ``LinearModelCV.fit`` from ``sklearn.linear_model._coordinate_descent``.

``LinearModelCV`` is an abstract base class, so every test exercises ``fit``
through one of its concrete subclasses (``LassoCV``, ``ElasticNetCV``,
``MultiTaskLassoCV`` and ``MultiTaskElasticNetCV``).
"""

import numbers
import warnings

import numpy as np
import pytest
import scipy.sparse as sp

import sklearn
from sklearn.exceptions import ConvergenceWarning, DataConversionWarning
from sklearn.linear_model import (
    ElasticNetCV,
    LassoCV,
    MultiTaskElasticNetCV,
    MultiTaskLassoCV,
)
from sklearn.linear_model._coordinate_descent import LinearModelCV
from sklearn.model_selection import GroupKFold, KFold
from sklearn.utils._testing import assert_allclose

MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS = [LassoCV, ElasticNetCV]
MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS = [MultiTaskLassoCV, MultiTaskElasticNetCV]


def _make_data(n_samples=40, n_features=4, n_targets=None, noise=0.1, seed=0):
    """Return a small, well conditioned regression problem."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)
    coef = np.zeros((n_features, n_targets if n_targets else 1))
    coef[0, :] = 2.0
    coef[-1, :] = -1.5
    if n_targets is not None:
        coef[:, 1] = -0.5 * coef[:, 0]
    y = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples, *(() if n_targets is None else (n_targets,)))
    if n_targets is None:
        y = y.ravel()
    return X, y


def test_documented_subclasses():
    """The concrete estimators used below really are LinearModelCV subclasses."""
    for Est in MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS + MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS:
        assert issubclass(Est, LinearModelCV)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_fit_returns_self_and_sets_attributes(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = Estimator(alphas=5, cv=4)

    returned = est.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is est
    # Fitted attributes are all present
    for attr in ("alpha_", "alphas_", "mse_path_", "coef_", "intercept_",
                 "dual_gap_", "n_iter_"):
        assert hasattr(est, attr), attr

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (5,)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (5, 4)
    assert est.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)
    assert np.isscalar(est.intercept_) or est.intercept_.shape == ()
    assert est.n_iter_ >= 1
    assert est.dual_gap_ >= 0
    # alpha_ is one of the evaluated alphas
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_
    # the CV errors are valid numbers
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(est.mse_path_))
    assert np.all(est.mse_path_ >= 0)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_fit_multitask_returns_self_and_sets_attributes(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    est = Estimator(alphas=5, cv=3)

    returned = est.fit(X, y)

    assert returned is est
    assert est.alphas_.shape == (5,)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (5, 3)
    assert est.coef_.shape == (2, X.shape[1])
    assert est.intercept_.shape == (2,)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(est.mse_path_))


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_alpha_is_the_minimizer_of_the_mean_cv_error(Estimator):
    """``alpha_`` must be the alpha with the lowest mean MSE over the folds."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = Estimator(alphas=7, cv=4).fit(X, y)

    mean_mse = est.mse_path_.mean(axis=1)
    assert mean_mse.shape == est.alphas_.shape
    assert est.alpha_ == est.alphas_[np.argmin(mean_mse)]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_alpha_is_the_minimizer_of_the_mean_cv_error_multitask(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    est = Estimator(alphas=6, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    mean_mse = est.mse_path_.mean(axis=1)
    assert est.alpha_ == est.alphas_[np.argmin(mean_mse)]


def test_l1_ratio_and_alpha_are_the_global_optimum():
    """With several ``l1_ratio`` values the best (l1_ratio, alpha) pair wins."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    l1_ratios = [0.7, 0.9, 1.0]
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=5, cv=4, l1_ratio=l1_ratios).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (len(l1_ratios), 5)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (len(l1_ratios), 5, 4)
    # every l1_ratio shares the same grid of alphas
    for alphas_row in est.alphas_:
        assert_allclose(alphas_row, est.alphas_[0])

    mean_mse = est.mse_path_.mean(axis=2)  # (n_l1_ratio, n_alphas)
    best_l1, best_alpha = np.unravel_index(np.argmin(mean_mse), mean_mse.shape)
    assert est.l1_ratio_ == l1_ratios[best_l1]
    assert est.alpha_ == est.alphas_[best_l1, best_alpha]


def test_mse_path_has_one_column_per_cv_fold():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    cv = KFold(n_splits=3)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=cv).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)

    cv = KFold(n_splits=6)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=cv).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 6)


def test_default_cv_is_five_fold():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=3).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (3, 5)


def test_integer_alphas_are_generated_as_a_decreasing_grid():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=8, eps=1e-2, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (8,)
    assert np.all(est.alphas_ > 0)
    assert np.all(np.diff(est.alphas_) < 0)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_user_provided_alphas_are_sorted_in_decreasing_order():
    X, y = _make_data()
    alphas = np.array([0.5, 0.001, 0.05, 0.01])
    est = LassoCV(alphas=alphas, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(est.alphas_, np.sort(alphas)[::-1])
    assert np.all(np.diff(est.alphas_) < 0)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_user_provided_alphas_with_several_l1_ratios_are_tiled():
    X, y = _make_data()
    alphas = [0.1, 0.01]
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=alphas, cv=3, l1_ratio=[0.5, 1.0]).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (2, 2)
    assert_allclose(est.alphas_[0], [0.1, 0.01])
    assert_allclose(est.alphas_[1], [0.1, 0.01])


def test_multiple_alphas_list_and_array_are_equivalent():
    X, y = _make_data()
    a = LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, 0.01, 0.001], cv=3).fit(X, y)
    b = LassoCV(alphas=np.array([0.1, 0.01, 0.001]), cv=3).fit(X, y)
    assert_allclose(a.alphas_, b.alphas_)
    assert_allclose(a.coef_, b.coef_)
    assert_allclose(a.mse_path_, b.mse_path_)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_l1_ratio_attribute_handling(Estimator):
    """``l1_ratio_`` is exposed only for estimators that have an ``l1_ratio``."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    if hasattr(est, "l1_ratio"):
        assert hasattr(est, "l1_ratio_")
        assert est.l1_ratio_ in np.atleast_1d(est.l1_ratio)
    else:

def test_l1_ratio_scalar_is_reported():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=4, cv=3, l1_ratio=0.4).fit(X, y)
    assert est.l1_ratio_ == 0.4
    assert est.alphas_.ndim == 1
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)


def test_mse_path_is_averaged_over_folds_unweighted():
    """``alpha_`` comes from the unweighted mean of the per-fold MSEs."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=4).fit(X, y)
    mean_mse = est.mse_path_.mean(axis=1)
    expected_idx = int(np.argmin(mean_mse))
    assert est.alpha_ == est.alphas_[expected_idx]


def test_sample_weight_of_ones_matches_no_weights():
    X, y = _make_data()
    unweighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    weighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(
        X, y, sample_weight=np.ones(X.shape[0])
    )
    assert weighted.alpha_ == unweighted.alpha_
    assert_allclose(weighted.coef_, unweighted.coef_)
    assert_allclose(weighted.mse_path_, unweighted.mse_path_)


def test_scalar_sample_weight_is_ignored():
    """A scalar ``sample_weight`` is a no-op (converted to ``None``)."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    assert isinstance(1.0, numbers.Number)
    unweighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    weighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y, sample_weight=1.0)
    assert weighted.alpha_ == unweighted.alpha_
    assert_allclose(weighted.coef_, unweighted.coef_)
    assert_allclose(weighted.mse_path_, unweighted.mse_path_)


def test_array_sample_weight_modifies_the_cv_path():
    X, y = _make_data()
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    sample_weight = 0.1 + rng.rand(X.shape[0])
    plain = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(X, y)
    weighted = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)

    assert_allclose(weighted.alphas_, plain.alphas_)
    assert not np.allclose(weighted.mse_path_, plain.mse_path_, rtol=1e-3)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_sample_weight_is_accepted_for_multitask(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    sample_weight = np.linspace(0.5, 2.0, X.shape[0])
    plain = Estimator(alphas=4, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    weighted = Estimator(alphas=4, cv=3).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(weighted.mse_path_))
    assert not np.allclose(weighted.mse_path_, plain.mse_path_, rtol=1e-3)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_alphas", [-1, 0, 1.5e-3])
def test_negative_or_zero_integer_alphas_are_rejected(bad_alphas):
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="alphas"):
        LassoCV(alphas=bad_alphas).fit(X, y)


def test_negative_alpha_in_a_list_is_rejected():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"alphas\[1\]"):
        LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, -1.0]).fit(X, y)


def test_non_numeric_alpha_in_a_list_is_rejected():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match=r"alphas\[1\]"):
        LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, "wrong"]).fit(X, y)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_multi_output_target_raises_for_mono_task_estimator(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="For multi-task outputs, use MultiTask"):
        Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_mono_output_target_raises_for_multitask_estimator(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="For mono-task outputs, use"):
        Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)


def test_single_column_2d_target_is_raveled():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.warns(DataConversionWarning, match="column-vector"):
        est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=3).fit(X, y.reshape(-1, 1))
    assert est.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)


def test_inconsistent_number_of_samples_raises():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="inconsistent numbers of samples"):
        LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y[:-1])


def test_nan_in_X_raises():
    X, y = _make_data()
    X = X.copy()
    X[0, 0] = np.nan
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="NaN"):
        LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)


def test_extra_fit_params_require_metadata_routing():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with sklearn.config_context(enable_metadata_routing=False):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="enable_metadata_routing"):
            LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y, groups=np.zeros(X.shape[0]))


def test_metadata_routing_forwards_groups_to_the_splitter():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    groups = np.repeat(np.arange(6), 5)
    with sklearn.config_context(enable_metadata_routing=True):
        est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=3)).fit(

    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_unknown_fit_param_with_routing_enabled_raises():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with sklearn.config_context(enable_metadata_routing=True):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="unexpected argument"):
            LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y, not_a_real_param=np.zeros(3))

    X, y = _make_data()
    X_original = X.copy()
    LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, copy_X=True).fit(X, y)
    assert np.array_equal(X, X_original)


def test_copy_X_false_gives_the_same_result():
    X, y = _make_data()
    reference = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, copy_X=True).fit(X, y)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, copy_X=False).fit(X.copy(), y)
    assert est.alpha_ == reference.alpha_
    assert_allclose(est.coef_, reference.coef_)
    assert_allclose(est.mse_path_, reference.mse_path_)


def test_fit_intercept_false_gives_zero_intercept():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, fit_intercept=False).fit(X, y)
    assert est.intercept_ == 0.0


def test_sparse_input_matches_dense_input():
    X, y = _make_data()
    dense = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(X, y)
    sparse = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(sp.csr_matrix(X), y)
    assert sparse.alpha_ == dense.alpha_
    assert_allclose(sparse.coef_, dense.coef_, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-7)
    assert_allclose(sparse.mse_path_, dense.mse_path_, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-7)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_multitask_sparse_input_raises(Estimator):
    """Multi-output targets are not supported together with sparse ``X``."""
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(sp.csr_matrix(X), y)


def test_list_input_arrays_are_accepted():
    X, y = _make_data()
    reference = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X.tolist(), y.tolist())
    assert est.alpha_ == reference.alpha_
    assert_allclose(est.coef_, reference.coef_)


def test_n_jobs_parallel_matches_serial():
    X, y = _make_data()
    serial = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=4, n_jobs=None).fit(X, y)
    parallel = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=4, n_jobs=2).fit(X, y)
    assert parallel.alpha_ == serial.alpha_
    assert_allclose(parallel.coef_, serial.coef_)
    assert_allclose(parallel.mse_path_, serial.mse_path_)


def test_repeated_fit_overwrites_the_fitted_attributes():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    first_alpha = est.alpha_
    first_coef = est.coef_.copy()

    X2, y2 = _make_data(seed=1, noise=1.0)
    est.fit(X2, 3.0 * y2)

    assert est.coef_.shape == first_coef.shape
    assert not np.allclose(est.coef_, first_coef)
    assert est.alpha_ != first_alpha


def test_selection_random_is_reproducible_with_random_state():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est1 = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, selection="random", random_state=0).fit(X, y)
    est2 = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, selection="random", random_state=0).fit(X, y)
    assert est1.alpha_ == est2.alpha_
    assert_allclose(est1.coef_, est2.coef_)


def test_positive_constraint_produces_non_negative_coefficients():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=3, positive=True).fit(X, y)
    assert np.all(est.coef_ >= 0)


def test_fit_does_not_emit_convergence_warning():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", ConvergenceWarning)
        est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, max_iter=5000).fit(X, y)

def test_fit_works_with_float32_input():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(
        X.astype(np.float32), y.astype(np.float32)
    )
    assert est.coef_.dtype == np.float32
    assert est.mse_path_.dtype == np.float32
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_refit_uses_the_selected_alpha():
    """The final model is refitted on the whole data with the best alpha."""
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=60, noise=0.5)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    residual = y - est.predict(X)
    assert np.mean(residual**2) < np.var(y)
    assert_allclose(est.coef_, est.coef_, rtol=0)  # arrays are plain ndarrays
    assert isinstance(est.coef_, np.ndarray)


def test_estimator_can_be_cloned_before_fit():
    """Cloning must not carry over state and produce the same result."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3)
    est.fit(X, y)
    clone = type(est)(**est.get_params())
    clone.fit(X, y)
    assert clone.alpha_ == est.alpha_
    assert_allclose(clone.coef_, est.coef_)

    est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=cv).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 6)


def test_default_cv_is_five_fold():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=3).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (3, 5)


def test_integer_alphas_are_generated_as_a_decreasing_grid():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=8, eps=1e-2, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (8,)
    assert np.all(est.alphas_ > 0)
    assert np.all(np.diff(est.alphas_) < 0)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_user_provided_alphas_are_sorted_in_decreasing_order():
    X, y = _make_data()
    alphas = np.array([0.5, 0.001, 0.05, 0.01])
    est = LassoCV(alphas=alphas, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(est.alphas_, np.sort(alphas)[::-1])
    assert np.all(np.diff(est.alphas_) < 0)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_user_provided_alphas_with_several_l1_ratios_are_tiled():
    X, y = _make_data()
    alphas = [0.1, 0.01]
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=alphas, cv=3, l1_ratio=[0.5, 1.0]).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (2, 2)
    assert_allclose(est.alphas_[0], [0.1, 0.01])
    assert_allclose(est.alphas_[1], [0.1, 0.01])


def test_multiple_alphas_list_and_array_are_equivalent():
    X, y = _make_data()
    a = LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, 0.01, 0.001], cv=3).fit(X, y)
    b = LassoCV(alphas=np.array([0.1, 0.01, 0.001]), cv=3).fit(X, y)
    assert_allclose(a.alphas_, b.alphas_)
    assert_allclose(a.coef_, b.coef_)
    assert_allclose(a.mse_path_, b.mse_path_)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_l1_ratio_attribute_handling(Estimator):
    """``l1_ratio_`` is exposed only for estimators that have an ``l1_ratio``."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    if hasattr(est, "l1_ratio"):
        assert hasattr(est, "l1_ratio_")
        assert est.l1_ratio_ in np.atleast_1d(est.l1_ratio)
    else:
        assert not hasattr(est, "l1_ratio_")
        assert est.l1_ratio_ if False else True  # pragma: no cover


def test_l1_ratio_scalar_is_reported():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=4, cv=3, l1_ratio=0.4).fit(X, y)
    assert est.l1_ratio_ == 0.4
    assert est.alphas_.ndim == 1
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)


def test_mse_path_is_averaged_over_folds_unweighted():
    """``alpha_`` comes from the unweighted mean of the per-fold MSEs."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=4).fit(X, y)
    mean_mse = est.mse_path_.mean(axis=1)
    expected_idx = int(np.argmin(mean_mse))
    assert est.alpha_ == est.alphas_[expected_idx]


def test_sample_weight_of_ones_matches_no_weights():
    X, y = _make_data()
    unweighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    weighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(
        X, y, sample_weight=np.ones(X.shape[0])
    )
    assert weighted.alpha_ == unweighted.alpha_
    assert_allclose(weighted.coef_, unweighted.coef_)
    assert_allclose(weighted.mse_path_, unweighted.mse_path_)


def test_scalar_sample_weight_is_ignored():
    """A scalar ``sample_weight`` is a no-op (converted to ``None``)."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    assert isinstance(1.0, numbers.Number)
    unweighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    weighted = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y, sample_weight=1.0)
    assert weighted.alpha_ == unweighted.alpha_
    assert_allclose(weighted.coef_, unweighted.coef_)
    assert_allclose(weighted.mse_path_, unweighted.mse_path_)


def test_array_sample_weight_modifies_the_cv_path():
    X, y = _make_data()
    rng = np.random.RandomState(0)
    sample_weight = 0.1 + rng.rand(X.shape[0])
    plain = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(X, y)
    weighted = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)

    assert_allclose(weighted.alphas_, plain.alphas_)
    assert not np.allclose(weighted.mse_path_, plain.mse_path_, rtol=1e-3)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_sample_weight_is_accepted_for_multitask(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    sample_weight = np.linspace(0.5, 2.0, X.shape[0])
    plain = Estimator(alphas=4, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    weighted = Estimator(alphas=4, cv=3).fit(X, y, sample_weight=sample_weight)
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(weighted.mse_path_))
    assert not np.allclose(weighted.mse_path_, plain.mse_path_, rtol=1e-3)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("bad_alphas", [-1, 0, 1.5e-3])
def test_negative_or_zero_integer_alphas_are_rejected(bad_alphas):
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="alphas"):
        LassoCV(alphas=bad_alphas).fit(X, y)


def test_negative_alpha_in_a_list_is_rejected():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r"alphas\[1\]"):
        LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, -1.0]).fit(X, y)


def test_non_numeric_alpha_in_a_list_is_rejected():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match=r"alphas\[1\]"):
        LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, "wrong"]).fit(X, y)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_multi_output_target_raises_for_mono_task_estimator(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="For multi-task outputs, use MultiTask"):
        Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_mono_output_target_raises_for_multitask_estimator(Estimator):
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="For mono-task outputs, use"):
        Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)


def test_single_column_2d_target_is_raveled():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.warns(DataConversionWarning, match="column-vector"):
        est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=3).fit(X, y.reshape(-1, 1))
    assert est.coef_.shape == (X.shape[1],)


def test_inconsistent_number_of_samples_raises():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="inconsistent numbers of samples"):
        LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y[:-1])


def test_nan_in_X_raises():
    X, y = _make_data()
    X = X.copy()
    X[0, 0] = np.nan
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="NaN"):
        LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)


def test_extra_fit_params_require_metadata_routing():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with sklearn.config_context(enable_metadata_routing=False):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="enable_metadata_routing"):
            LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y, groups=np.zeros(X.shape[0]))


def test_metadata_routing_forwards_groups_to_the_splitter():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    groups = np.repeat(np.arange(6), 5)
    with sklearn.config_context(enable_metadata_routing=True):
        est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=GroupKFold(n_splits=3)).fit(
            X, y, groups=groups
        )
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_unknown_fit_param_with_routing_enabled_raises():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with sklearn.config_context(enable_metadata_routing=True):
        with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="unexpected argument"):
            LassoCV(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y, not_a_real_param=np.zeros(3))


def test_copy_X_true_leaves_the_input_untouched():
    X, y = _make_data()
    X_original = X.copy()
    LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, copy_X=True).fit(X, y)
    assert np.array_equal(X, X_original)


def test_copy_X_false_gives_the_same_result():
    X, y = _make_data()
    reference = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, copy_X=True).fit(X, y)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, copy_X=False).fit(X.copy(), y)
    assert est.alpha_ == reference.alpha_
    assert_allclose(est.coef_, reference.coef_)
    assert_allclose(est.mse_path_, reference.mse_path_)


def test_fit_intercept_false_gives_zero_intercept():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, fit_intercept=False).fit(X, y)
    assert est.intercept_ == 0.0


def test_sparse_input_matches_dense_input():
    X, y = _make_data()
    dense = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(X, y)
    sparse = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=4).fit(sp.csr_matrix(X), y)
    assert sparse.alpha_ == dense.alpha_
    assert_allclose(sparse.coef_, dense.coef_, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-7)
    assert_allclose(sparse.mse_path_, dense.mse_path_, rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-7)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MULTI_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_multitask_sparse_input_raises(Estimator):
    """Multi-output targets are not supported together with sparse ``X``."""
    X, y = _make_data(n_targets=2)
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(sp.csr_matrix(X), y)


def test_list_input_arrays_are_accepted():
    X, y = _make_data()
    reference = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X.tolist(), y.tolist())
    assert est.alpha_ == reference.alpha_
    assert_allclose(est.coef_, reference.coef_)


def test_n_jobs_parallel_matches_serial():
    X, y = _make_data()
    serial = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=4, n_jobs=None).fit(X, y)
    parallel = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=4, n_jobs=2).fit(X, y)
    assert parallel.alpha_ == serial.alpha_
    assert_allclose(parallel.coef_, serial.coef_)
    assert_allclose(parallel.mse_path_, serial.mse_path_)


def test_repeated_fit_overwrites_the_fitted_attributes():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    first_alpha = est.alpha_
    first_coef = est.coef_.copy()

    X2, y2 = _make_data(seed=1, noise=1.0)
    est.fit(X2, 3.0 * y2)

    assert est.coef_.shape == first_coef.shape
    assert not np.allclose(est.coef_, first_coef)
    assert est.alpha_ != first_alpha


def test_selection_random_is_reproducible_with_random_state():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est1 = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, selection="random", random_state=0).fit(X, y)
    est2 = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, selection="random", random_state=0).fit(X, y)
    assert est1.alpha_ == est2.alpha_
    assert_allclose(est1.coef_, est2.coef_)


def test_positive_constraint_produces_non_negative_coefficients():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=6, cv=3, positive=True).fit(X, y)
    assert np.all(est.coef_ >= 0)


def test_fit_does_not_emit_convergence_warning():
    X, y = _make_data()
    with warnings.catch_warnings():
        warnings.simplefilter("error", ConvergenceWarning)
        est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, max_iter=5000).fit(X, y)
    assert est.n_iter_ <= 5000


def test_fit_works_with_float32_input():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(
        X.astype(np.float32), y.astype(np.float32)
    )
    assert est.coef_.dtype == np.float32
    assert est.mse_path_.dtype == np.float32
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_refit_uses_the_selected_alpha():
    """The final model is refitted on the whole data with the best alpha."""
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=60, noise=0.5)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    residual = y - est.predict(X)
    assert np.mean(residual**2) < np.var(y)
    assert_allclose(est.coef_, est.coef_, rtol=0)  # arrays are plain ndarrays
    assert isinstance(est.coef_, np.ndarray)


def test_estimator_can_be_cloned_before_fit():
    """Cloning must not carry over state and produce the same result."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3)
    est.fit(X, y)
    clone = type(est)(**est.get_params())
    clone.fit(X, y)
    assert clone.alpha_ == est.alpha_
    assert_allclose(clone.coef_, est.coef_)

def _make_data(n_samples=40, n_features=4, n_targets=None, noise=0.1, seed=0):
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    X = rng.randn(n_samples, n_features)

    coef[0, :] = 2.0
    coef[-1, :] = -1.5
    if n_out > 1:
        coef[:, 1] = -0.5 * coef[:, 0]
    y = X @ coef + noise * rng.randn(n_samples, n_out)
    if n_targets is None:
        return X, y.ravel()
    return X, y

messages.reasoning_content:
The file looks decent. Minor improvements:
- `test_estimator_can_be_cloned_before_fit` uses manual reconstruction instead of sklearn.base.clone — use clone from sklearn.base. It's cleaner and tests that clone doesn't carry state.

def test_l1_ratio_and_alpha_are_the_global_optimum():
    """With several ``l1_ratio`` values the best (l1_ratio, alpha) pair wins."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    l1_ratios = [0.7, 0.9, 1.0]
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=5, cv=4, l1_ratio=l1_ratios).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (len(l1_ratios), 5)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (len(l1_ratios), 5, 4)
    # one decreasing alpha grid per l1_ratio
    for alphas_row in est.alphas_:
        assert np.all(alphas_row > 0)
        assert np.all(np.diff(alphas_row) < 0)

    mean_mse = est.mse_path_.mean(axis=2)  # (n_l1_ratio, n_alphas)
    best_l1, best_alpha = np.unravel_index(np.argmin(mean_mse), mean_mse.shape)
    assert est.l1_ratio_ == l1_ratios[best_l1]
    assert est.alpha_ == est.alphas_[best_l1, best_alpha]


def test_mse_path_has_one_column_per_cv_fold():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    cv = KFold(n_splits=3)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=cv).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)

    cv = KFold(n_splits=6)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=4, cv=cv).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 6)


def test_default_cv_is_five_fold():
    X, y = _make_data(n_samples=30)
    est = LassoCV(alphas=3).fit(X, y)
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (3, 5)


def test_integer_alphas_are_generated_as_a_decreasing_grid():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = LassoCV(alphas=8, eps=1e-2, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    assert est.alphas_.shape == (8,)
    assert np.all(est.alphas_ > 0)
    assert np.all(np.diff(est.alphas_) < 0)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_user_provided_alphas_are_sorted_in_decreasing_order():
    X, y = _make_data()
    alphas = np.array([0.5, 0.001, 0.05, 0.01])
    est = LassoCV(alphas=alphas, cv=3).fit(X, y)

    assert_allclose(est.alphas_, np.sort(alphas)[::-1])
    assert np.all(np.diff(est.alphas_) < 0)
    assert est.alpha_ in est.alphas_


def test_user_provided_alphas_with_several_l1_ratios_are_tiled():
    X, y = _make_data()
    alphas = [0.1, 0.01]
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=alphas, cv=3, l1_ratio=[0.5, 1.0]).fit(X, y)

    # the same sorted grid is shared by all l1_ratio values, so it is stored 1d
    assert est.alphas_.shape == (2,)
    assert_allclose(est.alphas_, [0.1, 0.01])
    # one MSE path per l1_ratio, each with one column per fold
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (2, 2, 3)
    assert est.l1_ratio_ in [0.5, 1.0]


def test_multiple_alphas_list_and_array_are_equivalent():
    X, y = _make_data()
    a = LassoCV(alphas=[0.1, 0.01, 0.001], cv=3).fit(X, y)
    b = LassoCV(alphas=np.array([0.1, 0.01, 0.001]), cv=3).fit(X, y)
    assert_allclose(a.alphas_, b.alphas_)
    assert_allclose(a.coef_, b.coef_)
    assert_allclose(a.mse_path_, b.mse_path_)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("Estimator", MONO_TASK_ESTIMATORS)
def test_l1_ratio_attribute_handling(Estimator):
    """``l1_ratio_`` is exposed only for estimators that have an ``l1_ratio``."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = Estimator(alphas=3, cv=3).fit(X, y)
    if hasattr(est, "l1_ratio"):
        assert hasattr(est, "l1_ratio_")
        assert est.l1_ratio_ in np.atleast_1d(est.l1_ratio)
    else:
        assert not hasattr(est, "l1_ratio_")


def test_l1_ratio_scalar_is_reported():
    X, y = _make_data()
    est = ElasticNetCV(alphas=4, cv=3, l1_ratio=0.4).fit(X, y)
    assert est.l1_ratio_ == 0.4
    assert est.alphas_.ndim == 1
    assert est.mse_path_.shape == (4, 3)


def test_eps_controls_the_lower_bound_of_the_generated_grid():
    """``eps`` is the ratio between the smallest and the largest alpha."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    for eps in (1e-2, 1e-4):
        est = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, eps=eps).fit(X, y)
        assert_allclose(est.alphas_[-1], est.alphas_[0] * eps, rtol=1e-6)
        assert len(est.alphas_) == 5


def test_precompute_auto_matches_no_precompute():
    """``precompute="auto"`` is disabled on the final refitted model."""
    X, y = _make_data()
    auto = LassoCV(alphas=5, cv=3, precompute="auto").fit(X, y)

def test_l1_ratio_and_alpha_are_the_global_optimum():
    """With several ``l1_ratio`` values the best (l1_ratio, alpha) pair wins."""

    best_l1, best_alpha = np.unravel_index(np.argmin(mean_mse), mean_mse.shape)

def line_search(self, X, y, sample_weight):
        """Backtracking line search with Armijo condition.

        Backtracking line search with sufficient decrease condition, i.e. Armijo
        condition, is enough, no curvature condition needed, see Algorithm 3.1 of
        Nocedal & Wright 2nd ed.

        Define

            phi(alpha) = loss(coef_old + alpha * coef_newton)

        Searches for a step length alpha satisfying the sufficient decrease (Armijo)
        condition:

            phi(alpha) <= phi(0) + sigma * alpha * phi'(0)

        with sigma = 1/2 ** 11 ~ 5e-4.

        Sets:
            - self.coef_old
            - self.coef
            - self.loss_value_old
            - self.loss_value
            - self.gradient_old
            - self.gradient
            - self.raw_prediction
        """
        # line search parameters
        ls_converged = False
        sigma = 0.00048828125  # 1/2**11, sometimes called c1
        min_step_reduction = 1e-2  # minimum factor of decrease of alpha per step
        min_step_length = 1e-12  # absolute minimum value of alpha
        # Remember: dtype follows X, also the dtype of self.loss_value. For Array API
        # support, self.loss_value might be float instead of np.floatXX.
        eps = 16 * np.finfo(X.dtype).eps
        alpha = 1  # initial step size, Newton methods should always try 1 first.
        alpha_old = 1

        self.coef_old = self.coef
        self.loss_value_old = self.loss_value
        self.gradient_old = self.gradient
        phi_0 = phi_old = self.loss_value_old  # phi(0)
        phi_prime_0 = self.gradient_times_newton  # phi'(0) = gradient @ coef_newton

        # gradient_times_newton = self.gradient @ self.coef_newton
        # was computed in inner_solve.
        armijo_term = sigma * self.gradient_times_newton
        if self.l1_reg_strength > 0:
            # Add ||coef||_1 - ||coef_old||_1, see Eq. 2.19 and 2.14 of
            # Lee, Sun, Saunder (2012) "Proximal Newton-Type Methods".
            L1 = self.linear_loss.l1_penalty(
                self.coef + self.coef_newton, self.l1_reg_strength
            )
            L1_old = self.linear_loss.l1_penalty(self.coef_old, self.l1_reg_strength)
            armijo_term += sigma * (L1 - L1_old)

        _, _, raw_prediction_newton = self.linear_loss.weight_intercept_raw(
            self.coef_newton, X
        )

        # np.sum(np.abs(self.gradient_old))
        sum_abs_grad_old = -1

        is_verbose = self.verbose >= 2
        if is_verbose:
            print("  Backtracking Line Search")
            print(f"    eps=16 * finfo.eps={eps}")

        for i in range(21):
            self.coef = self.coef_old + alpha * self.coef_newton
            raw = self.raw_prediction + alpha * raw_prediction_newton
            self.loss_value, self.gradient = self.linear_loss.loss_gradient(
                coef=self.coef,
                X=X,
                y=y,
                sample_weight=sample_weight,
                l1_reg_strength=self.l1_reg_strength,
                l2_reg_strength=self.l2_reg_strength,
                n_threads=self.n_threads,
                raw_prediction=raw,
            )
            # Note: If coef_newton is too large, loss_gradient may produce inf values,
            # potentially accompanied by a RuntimeWarning.
            # This case will be captured by the Armijo condition.

            # 1. Check Armijo / sufficient decrease condition.
            # The smaller (more negative) the better.
            loss_improvement = self.loss_value - self.loss_value_old
            check = loss_improvement <= alpha * armijo_term
            if is_verbose:
                print(
                    f"    line search iteration={i + 1}, step size={alpha}\n"
                    f"      check loss improvement <= armijo term: {loss_improvement} "
                    f"<= {alpha * armijo_term} {check}"
                )
            if check:
                ls_converged = True
                break
            # 2. Tiny gradient / Armijo term.
            # If we are already close to the minimum, gradient and Armijo term are
            # tiny. It is best to use a Newton step length alpha = 1.
            if i == 0 and np.abs(armijo_term) <= self.tol:
                # Note that final convergence is checked with the infinity norm.
                mnsg = min_norm_subgradient(
                    self.l1_reg_strength, self.gradient, self.coef, self.linear_loss
                )  # equals gradient if l1_reg_strength = 0.
                g_max_abs = np.linalg.norm(mnsg.ravel(), ord=np.inf)
                check = g_max_abs <= self.tol
                if is_verbose:
                    print(
                        "      check max |gradient| <= tol: "
                        f"{g_max_abs} <= {self.tol} {check}"
                    )
                if check:
                    ls_converged = True
                    break
            # 3. Deal with differences around machine precision.
            # 3.1 Check relative loss difference ~ machine precision
            tiny_loss = np.abs(self.loss_value_old * eps)
            check = np.abs(loss_improvement) <= tiny_loss
            if is_verbose:
                print(
                    "      check loss |improvement| <= eps * |loss_old|:"
                    f" {np.abs(loss_improvement)} <= {tiny_loss} {check}"
                )
            if check:
                if sum_abs_grad_old < 0:
                    mnsg_old = min_norm_subgradient(
                        self.l1_reg_strength,
                        self.gradient_old,
                        self.coef_old,
                        self.linear_loss,
                    )
                    sum_abs_grad_old = np.linalg.norm(mnsg_old.ravel(), ord=1)
                # 3.2 Check sum of absolute gradients as alternative condition.
                mnsg = min_norm_subgradient(
                    self.l1_reg_strength, self.gradient, self.coef, self.linear_loss
                )  # equals gradient if l1_reg_strength = 0.
                sum_abs_grad = np.linalg.norm(mnsg.ravel(), ord=1)
                check = sum_abs_grad < sum_abs_grad_old
                if is_verbose:
                    print(
                        "      check sum(|gradient|) < sum(|gradient_old|): "
                        f"{sum_abs_grad} < {sum_abs_grad_old} {check}"
                    )
                if check:
                    ls_converged = True
                    break

            # Set a smart new value of alpha, smaller than previous one, larger than 0.
            # We know that
            #   - phi(0) = phi_0
            #   - phi(alpha) = phi_1
            #   - phi'(0) = phi_prime_0
            # We fit a quadratic polynomial through those 3 points and take the minimum
            # alpha as next trial step length.
            # See Nocedal & Wright 2nd ed. Chapter 3.5, page 58, Eq 3.58.
            phi_1 = self.loss_value
            alpha_trial = (
                -phi_prime_0 * alpha**2 / (2 * (phi_1 - phi_0 - phi_prime_0 * alpha))
            )
            if i > 0:
                # We additionally know phi(alpha_old) = phi_old and use cubic
                # interpolation.
                # See Nocedal & Wright 2nd ed. Chapter 3.5, page 58, below Eq 3.58.
                denom = (alpha_old * alpha) ** 2 * (alpha - alpha_old)
                vec0 = phi_1 - phi_0 - phi_prime_0 * alpha
                vec1 = phi_old - phi_0 - phi_prime_0 * alpha_old
                a = (alpha_old**2 * vec0 - alpha**2 * vec1) / denom
                b = (alpha**3 * vec1 - alpha_old**3 * vec0) / denom
                if a != 0 and b**2 - 3 * a * phi_prime_0 >= 0:
                    alpha_trial = (-b + math.sqrt(b**2 - 3 * a * phi_prime_0)) / (3 * a)
                # else we keep the quadratic alpha_trial from above

            alpha_old = alpha
            phi_old = phi_1
            # Safeguards
            if alpha_trial >= alpha or alpha_trial <= min_step_length:
                alpha_trial = 0.5 * alpha
            # Avoid too large a reduction of alpha.
            alpha = max(alpha_trial, min_step_reduction * alpha, min_step_length)
            if alpha == alpha_old:
                # For example if alpha = alpha_old = min_step_length.
                # The early exit avoids dividing by denom = 0 in the next iteration.
                break

        if not ls_converged:
            warnings.warn(
                (
                    f"Line search of Newton solver {self.__class__.__name__} at"
                    f" iteration #{self.iteration} did not converge after 21 line "
                    "search refinement iterations. It will now resort to lbfgs instead."
                ),
                ConvergenceWarning,
            )
            if self.verbose:
                print("  Line search did not converge and resorts to lbfgs instead.")
            self.use_fallback_lbfgs_solve = True
            return

        self.raw_prediction = raw
        if is_verbose:
            print(
                f"    line search successful after {i + 1} iterations with "
                f"loss={self.loss_value}."
            )

import math
import warnings

    enet_coordinate_descent,
    enet_coordinate_descent_gram,
    enet_coordinate_descent_multinomial,
    enet_coordinate_descent_sparse,
)
from sklearn.linear_model._linear_loss import (
    LinearModelLoss,
)
from sklearn.utils.fixes import _get_additional_lbfgs_options_dict
from sklearn.utils.optimize import _check_optimize_result


def min_norm_subgradient(alpha, gradient, coef, linear_loss):
    """Component-wise minimum norm subgradient of the loss function.

    The subgradient of f(x) + alpha ||x||_1 with the minimum L2 norm is defined
    component-wise, i.e. for component j:

        mn_sg(f(x) + alpha ||x||_1)_j =
            f'(x)_j + alpha                        if x_j > 0
            f'(x)_j - alpha                        if x_j < 0
            sign(f'(x)_j) max(|f'(x)_j| - alpha, 0)  if x_j = 0

    for positive alpha. See between equations (26) and (27) in
    Yuan, Ho, Lin (2011).

    Parameters
    ----------
    alpha : float
        The L1 penalty strength.

    gradient : ndarray of shape coef.shape
        The gradient of f(coef), i.e. f'(coef)

    coef : ndarray of shape (n_dof,) or (n_classes * n_dof,) or (n_classes, n_dof)

    linear_loss: LinearModelLoss
        Contains some meta information.

    Returns
    -------
    ndarray of shape gradient.shape

    References
    ----------
    - Yuan, G., Ho, C., & Lin, C. (2011). "An improved GLMNET for l1-regularized
      logistic regression." Journal of machine learning research.
      https://doi.org/10.1145/2020408.2020421
    """
    if alpha == 0:
        return gradient

    if gradient.shape != coef.shape or coef.ndim > 2:
        raise ValueError(
            "Shapes of 'gradient' and 'coef' must match, dimension must be smaller 3; "
            f"got {gradient.shape=} and {coef.shape=}."
        )
    if gradient.ndim == 1:
        result = gradient.copy()
    else:
        result = gradient.flatten(order="F")  # flatten returns a copy
        coef = coef.ravel(order="F")
    # mn_sgrad = minimum norm subgradient
    if linear_loss.fit_intercept:
        # For the intercept we just leave the gradient untouched.
        if linear_loss.base_loss.is_multiclass:
            n_classes = linear_loss.base_loss.n_classes
            mn_sgrad = result[:-n_classes]  # mn_sgrad is a view
        else:
            mn_sgrad = result[:-1]  # mn_sgrad is a view
    else:
        mn_sgrad = result
    weights, _ = linear_loss.weight_intercept(coef)
    # For multiclass, weights.shape = (n_classes, n_features), flatten again.
    if linear_loss.base_loss.is_multiclass:
        weights = weights.ravel(order="F")
    mn_sgrad[weights > 0] += alpha
    mn_sgrad[weights < 0] -= alpha
    mask = weights == 0
    mn_sgrad[mask] = np.sign(mn_sgrad[mask]) * np.fmax(
        np.abs(mn_sgrad[mask]) - alpha, 0
    )
    if gradient.ndim == 1:
        return result
    else:
        return result.reshape(gradient.shape, order="F")

      Cambridge University Press, 2004.
      https://web.stanford.edu/~boyd/cvxbook/bv_cvxbook.pdf

    - Lee, J., Sun, Y., & Saunders, M.A. (2012). "Proximal Newton-Type Methods for

      https://doi.org/10.1137/130921428
      https://arxiv.org/abs/1206.1623

    - Yuan, G., Ho, C., & Lin, C. (2011). "An improved GLMNET for l1-regularized

        Maximum number of Newton steps allowed.

    n_threads : int, default=1
        Number of OpenMP threads to use for the computation of the Hessian and gradient

    Attributes

    gradient : ndarray of shape coef.shape

    gradient_old : ndarray of shape coef.shape

    loss_value : float

    loss_value_old : float

        """Computes the sum of loss and gradient w.r.t. coef.

        Parameters
        ----------
        coef : ndarray of shape (n_dof,), (n_classes, n_dof) or (n_classes * n_dof,)
            Coefficients of a linear model.
            If shape (n_classes * n_dof,), the classes of one feature are contiguous,
            i.e. one reconstructs the 2d-array via
            coef.reshape((n_classes, -1), order="F").
        X : {array-like, sparse matrix} of shape (n_samples, n_features)
            Training data.
        y : contiguous array of shape (n_samples,)
            Observed, true target values.
        sample_weight : None or contiguous array of shape (n_samples,), default=None
            Sample weights.
        l1_reg_strength : float, default=0.0
            L1 regularization strength
        l2_reg_strength : float, default=0.0
            L2 regularization strength
        n_threads : int, default=1
            Number of OpenMP threads to use.
        raw_prediction : C-contiguous array of shape (n_samples,) or array of \
            shape (n_samples, n_classes)
            Raw prediction values (in link space). If provided, these are used. If
            None, then raw_prediction = X @ coef + intercept is calculated.

        Returns
        -------
        loss : float
            Weighted average of losses per sample, plus penalty.

        gradient : ndarray of shape coef.shape
             The gradient of the loss.
        """
        (n_samples, n_features), n_classes = X.shape, self.base_loss.n_classes
        n_dof = n_features + int(self.fit_intercept)

        if raw_prediction is None:
            weights, intercept, raw_prediction = self.weight_intercept_raw(coef, X)
        else:
            weights, intercept = self.weight_intercept(coef)

        loss, grad_pointwise = self.base_loss.loss_gradient(
            y_true=y,
            raw_prediction=raw_prediction,
            sample_weight=sample_weight,
            n_threads=n_threads,
        )
        xp, _ = get_namespace(X, y, sample_weight)
        sw_sum = n_samples if sample_weight is None else xp.sum(sample_weight)
        loss = float(xp.sum(loss) / sw_sum)
        if l1_reg_strength > 0:
            loss += self.l1_penalty(weights, l1_reg_strength)
        if l2_reg_strength > 0:
            loss += self.l2_penalty(weights, l2_reg_strength)

        grad_pointwise /= sw_sum

        # TODO: The lbfgs solver currently only works with numpy arrays and expects
        # both the coef argument and the result to be in numpy. So, for the time
        # being, we stick with a mix of numpy and array API. We could consider
        # moving coef to the device of X if lbgfs also becomes compatible with the
        # array API.
        if not self.base_loss.is_multiclass:
            grad = np.empty_like(coef, dtype=weights.dtype)
            X_grad = X.T @ grad_pointwise
            grad[:n_features] = (
                move_to(X_grad, xp=np, device="cpu") + l2_reg_strength * weights
            )
            if self.fit_intercept:
                grad[-1] = xp.sum(grad_pointwise)
        else:
            # The final value of `grad` needs to be in the `numpy` namespace
            # because the relevant `scipy.optimize` functions do not currently
            # support the array API.
            grad = np.empty((n_classes, n_dof), dtype=weights.dtype, order="F")

            grad_X = grad_pointwise.T @ X
            grad[:, :n_features] = (
                move_to(grad_X, xp=np, device="cpu") + l2_reg_strength * weights

            if self.fit_intercept:
                grad[:, -1] = move_to(

class NewtonCDSolver(NewtonSolver):
    """Coordinate Descent inner solver for a Newton solver.

    This solver can deal with L1 and L2 penalties.

    It avoids the explicit computation of hessian H = X' @ diag(h) @ X which makes it
    a good choice for use cases with n_features > n_samples (saves computation and
    saves large memory allocation of H).

    Inner solver for finding the Newton step

            H @ coef_newton = -G

    uses coordinate descent.
    With an L1 penalty, it is better to write down the minimization problem and use
    the 2nd order Taylor approximation only on the smooth parts (loss and L2), see
    Eq. 13 of Yuan, Ho, Lin (2011)

        min 1/2 d' H d + G' d + l1_reg ||coef + d||_1 - l1_reg ||coef||_1

    with d = coef_newton and coef = current coefficients.
    To circumvent the norm ||coef + d||_1, we instead minimize for
    c = coef_new = coef + d. This gives, up to constant terms

        min 1/2 c' H c + (G' - coef' H) c + l1_reg ||c||_1

    with
        c = coef_new = coef + coef_newton
        coef = current coefficients
        G = X.T @ g + l2_reg_strength * P @ coef
        H = X.T @ diag(h) @ X + l2_reg_strength * P
        g = loss.gradient = pointwise gradient
        h = loss.hessian = pointwise hessian
        P = penalty matrix in 1/2 w @ P @ w,
            for a pure L2 penalty without intercept it equals the identity matrix.

    Up to constant terms, this is then cast as a Lasso/Enet least squares problem with
    sample weights equal to the pointwise hessian

        min 1/2 ||diag(sqrt(h)) (X c - z)||_2^2 + l1_reg ||c||_1 + 1/2 l2_reg ||c||_2^2

    with

        z = -g/h + X coef

    Note: Defining
        A = diag(sqrt(h)) X
        b = sqrt(h) z = -g / sqrt(h) + diag(sqrt(h)) X coef
